provenance.audit: Each domain classification was audited for circularity by a second agent. Reported downgrade fractions ranged from 0.53 to 1.00 (mean about 0.74). The audits are stored in audits[] and their objection is sound: a classifier that already knows the outcome can read substrate off the indicator content. Only the dispensing-only and aggregate-sales classifications rest on documented properties of named national datasets and are therefore usable as stated.

rows.domain: Opioid prescribing safety
rows.instrument: HEDIS: Use of Opioids at High Dosage (HDO/UOD) and Risk of Continued Opioid Use (COU), NCQA
rows.basis: HEDIS is computed by health plans over their own administrative data. The drug events come from pharmacy claims, but the three named exclusion value sets (Malignant Neoplasms; Sickle Cell Anemia and HB-S Disease; Palliative Care) are diagnosis/procedure value sets and can only be evaluated against medical claims and encounter data, which the plan holds for adjudication. Rule shape is an overuse/avoidance rule: the numerator event is the presence of opioid dispensing at high dosage (or continued use), so deleting cancer/SCD/palliative still yields a publishable opioid rate. Cancer and sickle cell appear on medical claims because the payer needs them to adjudicate the encounter, not because of this rule; the palliative-care value set is partly HCPCS/CPT billing codes, also payment-facing.

rows.domain: Opioid prescribing safety
rows.instrument: eCQM CMS506v7 'Safe Use of Opioids – Concurrent Prescribing' (steward: CMS; used in Hospital IQR / Promoting Interoperability reporting)
rows.basis: An eCQM is by construction computed over the hospital's certified EHR data and reported as QRDA, not over a payer claims warehouse; the VSAC OIDs listed in the record are QDM Diagnosis/Medication elements. Inpatient encounter diagnoses are coded in that record for DRG billing as well as clinical use, so the condition is present for reasons independent of this rule; moderate rather than high because the CQL may draw on problem-list entries whose coding pressure is clinician-driven rather than billing-driven. Rule shape is avoidance (do not discharge on concurrent opioid + benzodiazepine); the cancer-pain, sickle-cell and OUD/MAT value sets name legitimate indications that remove patients from the numerator, and the discharge-prescribing rate remains computable without them.

rows.domain: Opioid prescribing safety
rows.instrument: Medicare Part D formulary-level opioid point-of-sale safety edits (7-day opioid-naive limit; 90 MME care-coordination edit; opioid+benzodiazepine edit; duplicative LA therapy edit)
rows.basis: These edits fire inside pharmacy claim adjudication at the point of sale. The transaction the edit runs on is an NCPDP pharmacy claim, which carries drug, quantity, days supply, prescriber and beneficiary but no diagnosis; Part D has no diagnosis field it can adjudicate against, which is why CMS authored no binding and delegated resolution to sponsors and pharmacist judgment. The exempted populations (cancer, sickle cell, hospice, palliative, long-term-care residents) are legitimate-indication carve-outs, and the edit still functions as a dose/duration rule without them. Hospice and LTC status are carried as enrollment/residence flags rather than as coded conditions, so no condition-coding pressure exists in this feed. Criterion shape recorded as avoidance for the suite as a whole, though the 90 MME edit is a soft care-coordination trigger closer to monitoring.

rows.domain: Opioid prescribing safety
rows.instrument: Medicare Part C & D Star Ratings — 'Use of Opioids at High Dosage in Persons Without Cancer' (OHD), 'Use of Opioids from Multiple Providers in Persons Without Cancer' (OMP), 'Use of Opioids at High Dosage and from Multiple Providers in Persons Without Cancer' (OHDMP)
rows.basis: CMS computes these centrally rather than from plan self-report: the drug axis is Prescription Drug Event data, and the cancer and hospice exclusions require Medicare FFS claims plus MA Encounter Data System diagnoses, which CMS holds. Moderate confidence because the PQA technical specification itself is member-restricted and was not reachable; the claim that the Patient Safety suite applies ICD-10 diagnosis codes alongside PQA NDC lists comes from CMS Part C & D technical notes, not from the PQA spec. Diagnoses in those feeds exist for claim adjudication and risk adjustment, independent of this measure. Avoidance rule; cancer names an indication that removes the patient from the numerator and the high-dosage rate survives its deletion.

rows.domain: Opioid prescribing safety
rows.instrument: National opioid prescribing comparators as implemented in the NHS prescribing-data measures used by ICBs ('High dose opioid items per 1000 patients'; 'High dose opioid items as percentage of regular opioids'; 'Total opioid prescribing as oral morphine equivalence')
rows.basis: These comparators are computed from NHSBSA dispensed-prescription data (ePACT2 / the same monthly practice-level prescribing dataset), with practice list size as the denominator. That feed is a reimbursement record for the dispensing contractor: it carries dm+d/BNF product, quantity and practice, and no patient diagnosis field at all, consistent with the recorded binding being SNOMED ingredient and dm+d vmp/vpi/ontformroute only. The underlying clinical rule (avoid high-dose opioids in chronic non-cancer pain) is an avoidance rule whose condition axis is a cancer/palliative indication carve-out; an opioid OME rate is publishable without it. No condition-coding pressure exists in the dispensing feed, whatever the GP record holds.

rows.domain: Opioid prescribing safety
rows.instrument: MFDS 의료용 마약류 진통제 안전사용 기준 (2021.5) — the national opioid prescribing standard, enforced against prescribers through the 마약류 사전알리미 notification mechanism
rows.basis: 사전알리미 is enforced by MFDS over the 마약류 통합관리시스템 (narcotics integrated management system) handling reports filed under the Narcotics Control Act, not over HIRA insurance claims. Those reports are a regulatory drug-custody feed carrying product, quantity, prescriber and patient identifier; they have no KCD/상병 field, which matches the recorded binding of ATC drug axis only with no KCD binding anywhere. Rule shape is avoidance of prescribing outside dose and duration ceilings; the standard separates cancer pain from non-cancer pain, so the condition axis is an indication carve-out and the prescriber-level exceedance count stands without it. Moderate confidence: I could not open the MFDS standard or the NIMS reporting schema this session to confirm the exact fields transmitted.

rows.domain: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant safety
rows.instrument: QOF Dataset and Business Rules - Atrial Fibrillation Indicator Set (AF), v34.0NI, DHSSPS Primary Care, 06/09/2016 (indicators AF001, AF006, AF007)
rows.basis: The instrument's own binding is Read v2 / CTV3 code clusters (AFIB_COD, CHADVASC_COD/_VAL, ORANTICOAG_COD) run against the GP practice clinical system record, which is what QOF business rules are executed over; that record carries coded diagnoses and risk-score values as ordinary general-practice recording, not for this rule. AF007 is an undertreatment rule (AF patients at CHA2DS2-VASc >=2 not on an anticoagulant), so the numerator is the absence of a drug and has no population without the AF register. Coding pressure: UK general-practice consultations are not diagnosis-adjudicated for payment and UK prescriptions are not reimbursed against an indication, so recording is clinical; the QOF register payment itself is part of this same instrument family and therefore not independent pressure.

rows.domain: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant safety
rows.instrument: NHS England Quality and Outcomes Framework, atrial fibrillation domain - AF001 register, AF006 (CHA2DS2-VASc assessment), AF007/AF008 (anticoagulation in CHA2DS2-VASc >=2); underpinned by NHS Digital Primary Care Domain refset AFIB_COD and the QOF business rules (v50, 2025)
rows.basis: Binding is SNOMED CT refsets/QOF code clusters published by the NHS England Digital Primary Care Domain and executed by the practice clinical system against the GP electronic record (extracted via GPES/CQRS). The GP record carries coded diagnoses and CHA2DS2-VASc values independently of this rule. AF007/AF008 is an undertreatment rule: numerator is absence of anticoagulation among AF patients at risk, so the AF register is the denominator and deleting it leaves nothing computable in that form. No diagnosis-linked payment adjudication of the encounter or of the prescription in England, so coding is clinician-recorded.

rows.domain: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant safety
rows.instrument: Polypharmacy Guidance: appropriate prescribing, making medicines safe, effective and sustainable 2026-2029, Appendix D / D1 - case finding indicators for clinical decision support deployed on the Scottish Therapeutics Utility (STU), specifications held in EScro (NHS National Services Scotland)
rows.basis: The stated binding is Read codes mapped to SNOMED CT plus dm+d, with specifications held in EScro; a binding of that shape can only execute against the GP clinical record, which is the feed STU reports run over inside the practice. That record carries coded diagnoses for ordinary clinical reasons. The AF case-finding indicator in this family is an undertreatment rule (AF and no anticoagulant), so the condition defines the population. Scottish general practice has no diagnosis-conditioned payment for the encounter and no indication-linked reimbursement of the prescription. I could not open the EScro specification itself, hence moderate.

rows.domain: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant safety
rows.instrument: Polypharmacy National Therapeutic Indicators (Appendix C of the same 2026-2029 guidance) - the national comparative prescribing indicator set
rows.basis: The Appendix C National Therapeutic Indicator set is computed nationally from the Prescribing Information System, a dispensed-prescription feed; the sibling record for the same Appendix C document in this dataset states its binding as 'Prescription/dispensing data only (Prescribing Information System)'. PIS carries prescriber, patient identifier, drug and quantity and no clinical diagnosis, and there is no payer requirement to attach a condition to a Scottish prescription. criterionShape and conditionRole are recorded for the underlying clinical criterion (anticoagulation in AF), which is an undertreatment rule whose numerator is a drug absence; note that as published the Appendix C indicator is a drug-volume/drug-choice comparator, so the load-bearing judgement is about the clinical criterion and not about the arithmetic this instrument actually publishes.

rows.domain: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant safety
rows.instrument: CMS Quality Payment Program, MIPS Quality ID #326: Atrial Fibrillation and Atrial Flutter: Chronic Anticoagulation Therapy (MIPS CQM, Version 10.0, December 2025, for the 2026 performance period; measure stewarded by ACC/AHA)
rows.basis: The stated binding is an ICD-10-CM denominator diagnosis list plus HCPCS G-codes for the exclusions and the CHA2DS2-VASc result; both are billing-data constructs, and the denominator is assembled from billed professional encounters (ICD-10 plus CPT encounter codes) even when submitted through a qualified registry rather than as a Part B claims measure. A US professional claim will not adjudicate without a diagnosis, and nonvalvular AF is a risk-adjusted (HCC) condition, so the condition is coded for payment reasons independent of this rule. The rule is undertreatment: AF/flutter patients at thromboembolic risk not prescribed an anticoagulant. Moderate because I could not open the v10.0 specification to confirm which collection-type feed is authoritative for 2026.

rows.domain: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant safety
rows.instrument: HIRA 요양급여 적정성평가, 급성기뇌졸중 (acute stroke) indicator STR0020 '심방세동이 있는 환자의 항응고제 퇴원처방률' (anticoagulant discharge prescription rate in patients with atrial fibrillation), as specified in HIRA's 2020 평가지표 상세설명서 모음집
rows.basis: The record states the data source explicitly: 의무기록자료 (조사표), a HIRA-authored chart-abstraction survey, with KCD I63 used only for the population frame. substrateCarriesCondition is false because the atrial-fibrillation field exists on that abstraction form because this assessment created it, not for a reason independent of the rule; the underlying medical record contains AF but the computed feed is the purpose-built 조사표. codingPressure is separately reimbursement-justifying: Korean claims carry mandatory KCD 상병명 for adjudication and Korean benefit criteria for DOACs require a documented non-valvular AF indication, so AF here is an indication-type (carve-in) condition. Rule shape is undertreatment. Moderate because I could not re-open the 상세설명서 to confirm the 2020 조사표 field list.

rows.domain: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant safety
rows.instrument: HIRA 급성기뇌졸중 indicator STR0021 '항혈전제 퇴원처방률' (antithrombotic discharge prescription rate) - the sibling indicator without the AF condition
rows.basis: Same computation feed as STR0020: KCD I63 population frame plus a HIRA chart-abstraction 조사표. Here the condition axis in play is the acute ischaemic stroke diagnosis itself, which is carried as a mandatory KCD code on the Korean inpatient claim for adjudication, independently of this indicator, so substrateCarriesCondition is true for the condition this instrument actually uses. The clinical rule is undertreatment (ischaemic stroke patients discharged without an antithrombotic); the stroke diagnosis is the denominator and no measure exists without it. Moderate: the split between claims-derived population frame and abstracted numerator detail is stated in the record but I could not verify field-level provenance in the primary document.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: CMS MDS 3.0 Quality Measure N047.01, 'Percent of Residents Who Received an Antipsychotic Medication (Long Stay)' (CMIT 526), as re-specified in QM User's Manual V18.0 effective 2026-01-01
rows.basis: Primary computation substrate is the MDS 3.0 resident assessment submitted to CMS (drug receipt from Section N; conditions from Section I items I6000/I5350/I5250), which the dataset's own binding string names. MDS Section I is a mandated active-diagnosis section completed for every resident for care planning and case-mix classification, i.e. it predates and is independent of this measure. Coded 'registry' rather than claims because the assessment is the core feed; the V18.0 respecification adds an ICD-10-CM exclusion list read from Medicare/Medicaid claims, so the substrate is genuinely hybrid - not established which side dominates in volume. Coding pressure coded 'clinically-recorded-only' because no payer requires schizophrenia/Tourette's/Huntington's to be recorded for an antipsychotic to be paid; whether PDPM case-mix creates independent pressure on these specific items is not established.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: CMS MDS 3.0 Quality Measure N011.03, 'Percent of Residents Who Newly Received an Antipsychotic Medication (Short Stay)' (CMIT 1183)
rows.basis: Same MDS 3.0 assessment feed as N047.01 but, per the dataset's binding string, with no claims-side ICD list, so the substrate is purely the mandated assessment. Section I diagnosis items exist for care planning/case-mix independent of this measure. Denominator is all short-stay residents with the named diagnoses removing residents from the measured population, hence exclusion-carveout. No payer requirement establishes reimbursement pressure on these three diagnoses.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: CMS Part D Patient Safety measure DMD08 'Antipsychotic Use in Persons with Dementia (APD)' and DMD09 'APD for Long-Term Nursing Home Residents (APD-LTNH)', 2026 Part C & D Display Measure Technical Notes
rows.basis: Dataset's own binding string states the PQA ICD-10-CM value sets are applied by CMS to Common Working File and Encounter Data System diagnoses, i.e. Part A/B claims and MA encounters, while the drug side comes from Part D PDE. Those claim feeds carry ICD-10-CM because a diagnosis is required for the encounter to adjudicate and for risk adjustment, independent of this rule. Condition role coded severable because deleting the dementia denominator still leaves a computable antipsychotic-use rate; note the instrument carries a second condition axis (APP_IND_ANTIPSYCHOTIC_USE, MAJOR_DEPRESSION) that is an exclusion-carveout, so this row compresses two structurally different roles into the dominant one.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: Medicare Part D Star Ratings measure set (drives Quality Bonus Payments) - the antipsychotic-in-dementia measure is absent from it
rows.basis: Negative-space row: the instrument recorded is the absence of the measure, so there is no computable definition to inspect and conditionRole is not-applicable by construction rather than by evidence. Substrate coded from the fact that Part D patient-safety Star measures are computed from prescription drug event records, which carry NDC, dates and quantity but no diagnosis field. The wider Star Ratings set also contains Part C measures computed on claims with diagnoses; that mixture is not resolved here, hence low confidence.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: 42 CFR 483.45(e) Psychotropic Drugs, survey tag F758, CMS State Operations Manual Appendix PP (enforcement; non-compliance carries denial of payment and civil money penalties under 42 CFR 488.406)
rows.basis: The regulation text quoted in the dataset ('a specific condition as diagnosed and documented in the clinical record') makes the surveyor's read of the resident's clinical record the substrate; there is no value set and no electronic feed. The record documents diagnoses for care reasons independent of this rule and a surveyor can adjudicate them by reading, so substrateCarriesCondition is true in the narrative sense, not in a coded sense. Coded exclusion-carveout because a documented indication removes the case from the deficiency set; this instrument publishes no rate, so the 'still leaves a publishable drug rate' test does not apply cleanly.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: CIHI indicator 'Potentially Inappropriate Use of Antipsychotics in Long-Term Care'
rows.basis: Dataset's binding string names RAI-MDS 2.0 and interRAI LTCF assessment items plus ICD-10 codes for Huntington's, which places the computation on CIHI's continuing-care assessment submissions rather than on physician claims. Those assessments are mandated for all residents in participating jurisdictions for care planning and case-mix, independent of this indicator. Denominator is all LTC residents with psychosis-type diagnoses removing residents, hence exclusion-carveout. I could not open the CIHI indicator specification this session (the URL I tried returned 404), so the exact exclusion list is not established.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: NICE indicator IND12, 'Dementia: anti-psychotic prescriptions'
rows.basis: Dataset states NICE authored no binding and delegates it to the NHS England Primary Care Dementia Data collection, which is an extract from GP clinical systems; that is the ground for coding the substrate as a primary-care EHR extract, and GP records carry coded dementia diagnoses and prescribing independent of this indicator. Coding pressure coded reimbursement-justifying because dementia is a QOF register condition that practices are paid to maintain, but that is payment for register maintenance rather than claim adjudication, so the fit to the enum is imperfect. The analyst who logged this row could not obtain the underlying specification and neither could I, hence low confidence throughout.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: Public Health Scotland National Therapeutic Indicators (NTIs), including NTI 8e / NTI 8ea 'Antipsychotics (older people %)', CHNTI 8ea 'Antipsychotics (care home residents aged 50+ %)', NTI 8pf / CHNTI 8pf 'antipsychotic in combination with two other drugs of dependence'
rows.basis: The NTIs are computed nationally from the Prescribing Information System, a dispensed-prescription feed holding drug, quantity, prescriber, patient identifier, age and sex but no diagnosis; the dataset's own binding string confirms drug-side BNF/prescription data plus an age threshold and a care-home residency definition. Nothing in that feed carries a patient condition, so there is no coding pressure of any kind on the dispensing record. Avoidance rule, and deleting the condition still yields a publishable antipsychotic rate.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: HIRA 요양병원 입원급여 적정성평가 process indicator '항정신성의약품 처방률' (antipsychotic prescribing rate), 2024 (2주기6차) detailed implementation plan
rows.basis: HIRA 적정성평가 indicators for 요양병원 are computed from submitted 요양급여비용 청구자료, which mandatorily carry KCD 주상병/부상병 because HIRA will not adjudicate a claim without them; the dataset's own binding note confirms 주상병 is present in the feed and is used, as a case-mix adjuster inside the Prescription Index. Substrate classification therefore rests on the claim feed's structure, not on whether the condition was used as a criterion. Avoidance shape, and the drug rate is computable without any condition, hence severable.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: MHLW 診療報酬 向精神薬多剤投与 減算 (payment reduction for multi-drug psychotropic prescribing), with quarterly reporting on 別紙様式40 to the Regional Bureau of Health and Welfare
rows.basis: The reduction is applied when the レセプト is adjudicated, and Japanese receipts carry a mandatory 傷病名 field against which prescribed drugs are matched, so the feed carries conditions in adjudicable form for reasons independent of this rule. criterionShape coded 'other' because the clinical rule here is a concurrent-drug-count cap (>=3 antipsychotics etc.), not an avoidance rule naming a patient condition; calling it avoidance would require a condition axis the rule does not have. conditionRole is the weak point: the criterion has no condition term at all, and I coded severable-refinement on the reasoning that any indication qualifier could be deleted while leaving a computable drug-count rate; 'not-applicable' is a defensible alternative and I could not settle it from a document.

rows.domain: Antipsychotic use in dementia
rows.instrument: National Aged Care Mandatory Quality Indicator Program, 'Medication management - antipsychotics' quality indicator (residential aged care), results published quarterly by AIHW GEN
rows.basis: Dataset records that the determination is made by the provider from its own clinical records ('a diagnosed condition of psychosis'), which is the point at which the condition is adjudicated, so I coded the substrate as chart-review-narrative; the onward feed to the department and AIHW is aggregate provider self-report, so 'self-report' is a defensible alternative label and the QI Program Manual was not reachable this session. Aged-care clinical records document psychosis diagnoses for care reasons independent of this indicator, but no payer requires that diagnosis inside this feed, so coding pressure is clinically-recorded-only; note that PBS restrictions on some antipsychotics create indication pressure in a different feed the indicator does not run on.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: HIRA 급성상기도감염(J00-J06) 항생제처방률 — acute upper respiratory infection antibiotic prescribing rate, 약제급여 적정성 평가
rows.basis: HIRA 적정성평가 for 약제 is computed over 요양급여비용 청구명세서 (NHI claim records), which mandatorily carry KCD 상병코드 (주/부상병) because HIRA will not adjudicate a claim without them; the record's own binding states the KCD J00–J06 range sits inside the indicator definition. Severability: the numerator event is an antibiotic prescription, so deleting J00–J06 still yields a publishable antibiotic prescribing rate over all outpatient claims (which is exactly what the England comparator publishes).

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: HIRA 급성상기도감염 항생제처방률 — 등급 공개 (public 1–5 grade disclosure, absolute thresholds)
rows.basis: Grading layer applied to the same claims-computed rate; no separate data collection. Same KCD binding inherited per the record. Coding pressure is the general NHI adjudication requirement for 상병코드, independent of this stewardship rule.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: HIRA 의원급 외래 약제적정성평가 가감지급사업 (pay-for-performance bonus/penalty) using 급성상기도감염 항생제처방률
rows.basis: Payment adjustment computed from the same 청구명세서-derived indicator; the P4P layer adds thresholds, not a new feed. Diagnosis coding on the claim is required for adjudication of the encounter regardless of this programme.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: HIRA 급성상기도감염 광범위 항생제처방률 (3rd-gen+ cephalosporin, quinolone, macrolide share within J00-J06)
rows.basis: Same claims substrate; record states KCD J00–J06 for the denominator plus drug-class binding for the numerator. Deleting the condition leaves a broad-spectrum share of all antibiotic prescribing, a rate published elsewhere (ESAC-Net analogue), so the condition is a refinement rather than the only possible population.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: HIRA 급성하기도감염(J20-J22) 항생제 처방률 (acute lower respiratory infection), added 2020
rows.basis: Same 청구명세서 substrate and same mandatory KCD coding; the J20–J22 range appears in the indicator name per the record. Numerator is a drug event, so a condition-free antibiotic rate remains computable.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: 의료질평가지원금 (Healthcare Quality Assessment Support Fund) linkage of 항생제·주사제처방률
rows.basis: Institution-level payment fund that ingests HIRA appropriateness-evaluation results, which are themselves computed over NHI claims carrying mandatory KCD codes; the record notes 'inherited HIRA KCD bindings'. Moderate rather than high because I could not reach the fund's own indicator specification to confirm whether the antibiotic component is re-specified or taken as a delivered score.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: NHS England Quality Premium 2015/16 — 'Improved antibiotic prescribing in primary and secondary care'
rows.basis: Computed from NHSBSA prescribing/dispensing data (items per STAR-PU, BNF 5.1 sub-sections per the record's own binding) plus secondary-care antibiotic consumption; that feed contains no patient diagnosis at all. RTI diagnoses do exist in English GP EHRs but are recorded by clinician choice, not because any payer requires them to reimburse an antibiotic. Numerator is a dispensed item, so a pure drug rate is publishable without any condition.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: NHS Pharmacy First advanced service (community pharmacy, 2023/24 onward) — seven condition-specific clinical pathways with antibiotic supply under PGD
rows.basis: The service fee is claimed per clinical pathway, so the pathway (condition) is on the payment record and the consultation is recorded and transmitted to the GP record; the record describes NHSE-authored pathways with gateway points and condition-specific PGDs rather than a diagnosis code list. Load-bearing because the instrument is a per-condition supply gate, not a rate: delete the condition and there is no pathway, no PGD and no claimable fee. Moderate confidence because I could not open the service specification to confirm the exact claim data elements.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: MHLW 抗微生物薬適正使用の手引き 第三版 (national antimicrobial stewardship manual)
rows.basis: Not a computed instrument: it fires at the point of care against the clinician's own diagnostic assessment, which is the record in front of them, so the 'feed' trivially contains the condition. Coded as chart-review-narrative for want of a better enum value; substrate confidence is low because there is no data feed to establish. Coding pressure recorded as reimbursement-justifying on the jurisdiction-level fact that Japanese レセプト require a 傷病名 for the encounter and the drug to be paid. Shape is avoidance (no antibiotic for J00–J06 / A00–A09 presentations) and a condition-free antibiotic-volume statement would still be publishable.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: 耳鼻咽喉科小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 (ENT paediatric antimicrobial stewardship support add-on), 80 points once monthly
rows.basis: Adjudicated on the レセプト, whose 傷病名 field is mandatory for any claim to be paid and is maintained as a separate standard master, exactly as the record states. Load-bearing because the add-on is a per-condition service fee: with the condition deleted there is no claimable event at all (the paid act is 'diagnosed acute URI/diarrhoea and did not prescribe an antibiotic'). Moderate because the fee notice states disease names in prose and I could not confirm which 傷病名 master codes insurers accept.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: 抗菌薬適正使用体制加算 (antimicrobial appropriate-use system add-on), new in the FY2024 fee revision
rows.basis: The qualifying test is a facility-level share of WHO AWaRe 'Access' agents within total antimicrobial use, i.e. an aggregate drug-consumption count with no patient row and therefore no condition; 'aggregate-sales' is the closest enum for facility-level consumption totals and substrate confidence is accordingly low. Coding pressure is the jurisdiction-level レセプト 傷病名 requirement, which exists but is not carried into this aggregate feed. Drug-mix rate is publishable without any condition.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: 感染対策向上加算１ — antimicrobial stewardship team (AST) duty (オ) within the facility standard for the fee add-on
rows.basis: A 施設基準 duty discharged by the AST reviewing individual inpatient records and verified by 届出 and on-site audit rather than by any computation; the record notes natural-language condition names, no codes and no threshold. The chart contains conditions for ordinary clinical reasons. Severable because the duty to monitor targeted antimicrobial use survives deletion of the condition wording. Low confidence throughout: I could not reach the facility-standard notification text.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: NCQA HEDIS 'Avoidance of Antibiotic Treatment for Acute Bronchitis/Bronchiolitis' (AAB), as adopted by CMS as Adult Core Set measure AAB-AD
rows.basis: Value sets named in the record are ICD-10-CM/ICD-9-CM/CPT/HCPCS/UB revenue codes, which only exist on submitted claims and encounter data; a payer will not adjudicate without a diagnosis. Denominator condition is acute bronchitis; the Comorbid Conditions and Competing Diagnosis value sets are true exclusion carve-outs sitting alongside it, so this row's single conditionRole understates a mixed structure. Severable in the schema's sense because the numerator event is a dispensed antibiotic and a condition-free dispensing rate remains publishable. Moderate: the NCQA measure page returned HTTP 403 and I could not confirm whether the current HEDIS year is administrative or ECDS.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: NCQA HEDIS public reporting / health plan report cards using the antibiotic-avoidance measures
rows.basis: Reporting layer over plan-submitted HEDIS rates computed on the same administrative claims/encounter substrate and the same NCQA value sets; no independent data collection. Same 403 limitation as the underlying measure row.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: CMS Medicaid/CHIP Core Set reporting (state-level quality reporting to CMS)
rows.basis: States compute Core Set rates from Medicaid MMIS/T-MSIS claims and encounter data, which carry ICD-10-CM diagnoses because the state will not pay a claim without them; the record states the NCQA value sets are adopted wholesale, and those value sets are claims code systems. Moderate because I could not open the CMS technical specification for the reporting year.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) Authority Required restrictions on antibiotics — e.g. norfloxacin (item 3010K)
rows.basis: Fetched pbs.gov.au/medicine/item/3010K directly: norfloxacin is Authority Required with two structured Indications fields, 'Acute bacterial enterocolitis' and 'Complicated urinary tract infection', and no additional treatment-phase criteria. The indication is stated by the prescriber and captured in the authority/streamlined-authority approval attached to the PBS claim, so the condition is present in adjudicable form purely because subsidy requires it, in a PBS-specific vocabulary rather than ICD or SNOMED. Load-bearing because the instrument is a subsidy gate whose entire content is the indication: delete it and the listing is simply unrestricted, leaving no rule. Moderate because I did not open the Schedule's authority-processing documentation to confirm how the indication is stored for non-streamlined authorities.

rows.domain: Antimicrobial stewardship and appropriate antibiotic prescribing
rows.instrument: ESAC-Net antimicrobial consumption surveillance and its published quality indicators
rows.basis: Countries report aggregated antimicrobial consumption to ECDC as DDD per 1000 inhabitants per day, derived from national sales or reimbursement totals; the record's binding is ATC to the 4th level, drug axis only. An aggregate consumption total has no patient row and therefore cannot carry a condition. Coding pressure marked unknown because the network spans ~30 national systems with different reimbursement rules and no single answer can be established.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: NHSBSA / NHS England Valproate Safety Implementation Group — Valproate Safety Dashboard (indicators VPA1–VPA5), ePACT2 and Catalyst
rows.basis: Instrument names its own delivery platforms (ePACT2 / Catalyst), which are NHSBSA dispensed-prescription warehouses built from processed prescription forms, and the stated binding is BNF presentation codes plus Patient Demographic Service sex and age. A dispensing feed carries prescriber, patient identifier, drug and quantity; it carries no clinical condition field of any kind. Rule shape is avoidance (valproate to be avoided in patients able to become pregnant absent the ACBS/pregnancy-prevention conditions), so a drug-side rate over a demographic denominator remains computable without any pregnancy variable. No payer in England requires pregnancy or childbearing potential to be coded for valproate to be reimbursed. Could not open the VPA1–VPA5 specification document itself (web search budget exhausted); substrate read from the platform named in the instrument title.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: NHSBSA Antimicrobial Stewardship Dashboard – Children (comparators ASC01–ASC05)
rows.basis: Same NHSBSA prescribing-data platform family as the valproate dashboard; the stated binding is BNF drug groupings plus age bands, which is the signature of a dispensing feed with a demographic join and no clinical field. Underlying clinical rule for paediatric antimicrobial stewardship is avoidance (do not give antibiotics for self-limiting childhood infection), which leaves a publishable antibiotic-items-per-child rate when the infection axis is deleted. Could not open the ASC01–ASC05 comparator definitions, so criterion shape is inferred from the stewardship subject matter rather than from a read denominator; marked moderate for that reason.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: All Wales National Prescribing Indicators 2025–2028 (and 2022–2025), All Wales Prescribing Advisory Group / AWTTC, endorsed by the All Wales Medicines Strategy Group
rows.basis: The AWTTC NPI set is a mixed-feed programme: most comparative indicators are computed from Welsh primary care prescribing/dispensing data at practice level, while at least one safety indicator in the same programme is documented as reading numeric eGFR and register membership from the DHCW GP record. I could not open the 2025–2028 specification to establish which feed the pregnancy/teratogen and paediatric indicators actually run on, and I decline to guess, so substrate and coding pressure are unknown. Criterion shape is classifiable independently: teratogen-in-pregnancy and antibiotic-in-children indicators are avoidance rules, and an avoidance rule still yields a publishable drug-side rate with the condition removed.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: MFDS/KIDS 임부금기 (pregnancy-contraindicated ingredients) operated through the national DUR system
rows.basis: The DUR check fires on the prescription/dispensing transaction transmitted to HIRA in real time at the moment of prescribing or dispensing; the KCD diagnosis lives on the 요양급여 claim, which is a separate, later submission and is not part of the DUR transaction. The instrument's own binding confirms this shape: drug axis bound at ingredient (성분) level, pregnancy carried as a transmitted binary 임부여부 flag entered by the prescriber. A clinician-entered flag on a transaction is not an adjudicated coded condition and exists only because this rule asks for it, so substrateCarriesCondition is false and coding pressure is none. Shape is avoidance; deleting pregnancy leaves an ingredient-level alert/rate that is still computable, though clinically meaningless, hence severable rather than load-bearing — moderate confidence because the severability test fits a rate-style instrument better than an alert-style one.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: MFDS/KIDS 특정연령대금기 (age-contraindicated ingredients) in the national DUR system
rows.basis: Same DUR prescription-transaction substrate as 임부금기: fires on the transmitted prescription line, no diagnosis present. The stated binding is ingredient name plus an age threshold plus dosage form. The second axis of this criterion is chronological age, which is a demographic attribute and not a patient condition at all, so conditionRole is not-applicable rather than severable — there is no condition in the source clinical rule for an instrument to retain or drop. Coding pressure is none for the same reason.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: HIRA 약제급여 적정성 평가 (Medication Benefit Appropriateness Evaluation) — paediatric antibiotic prescribing-rate indicators
rows.basis: 약제급여 적정성평가 is computed by HIRA over 요양급여비용 청구명세서 (the national fee-for-service claims file). The 상병코드 (KCD) field is mandatory on that claim for HIRA to adjudicate and pay it, entirely independent of any appropriateness indicator, so the feed carries the condition in adjudicable form and coding pressure is reimbursement-justifying. Underlying rule is avoidance (do not give antibiotics for self-limiting paediatric respiratory infection); deleting the KCD range still leaves a publishable antibiotic prescribing rate per claim, so the condition is a severable refinement of the denominator rather than the only thing that makes a numerator countable.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: 小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 and 耳鼻咽喉科小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 (paediatric antimicrobial-stewardship support add-on, 80 points), MHLW fee schedule
rows.basis: The add-on is claimed on the レセプト and adjudicated by the review bodies against that claim. 傷病名 is a mandatory field on every Japanese health-insurance receipt for the claim to be paid at all, so the feed carries a condition in adjudicable form for reasons wholly independent of this stewardship rule — that is textbook reimbursement-justifying pressure, and the instrument's own binding note says exactly that (prose disease names in the fee notice, adjudicated against the standard 傷病名 master). Rule shape is avoidance: the fee pays for explaining and NOT prescribing an antibiotic in acute paediatric respiratory/diarrhoeal illness. Severability is the weaker call here: it is a fee item rather than a rate, and stripping the condition would leave a payable-but-meaningless add-on, so I marked severable per the arithmetic definition and flag the fit as imperfect.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: 妊婦加算 (pregnancy consultation add-on), created in the FY2018 fee revision, frozen from 2019-01-01 and absent from the FY2024 fee schedule
rows.basis: Substrate is the レセプト, since the add-on was a fee-schedule item billed and adjudicated on the claim. Whether that feed carried pregnancy in adjudicable form is genuinely unresolved and I mark it null rather than guess: 傷病名 is mandatory in general, but normal pregnancy is not an insured condition under Japanese health insurance (antenatal care runs outside the fee schedule), so pregnancy is not reliably present as an adjudicated disease name on a medical receipt, and I could not open the fee notice to check whether any 記載 requirement was imposed. Coding pressure is unknown for the same reason. Shape is 'other': this is a consultation-fee uplift for extra care and prescribing caution in pregnancy, not a computable avoidance, dosing or monitoring criterion. ConditionRole is load-bearing because pregnancy is the entire billing eligibility — remove it and no instrument remains. Classified as specified, without regard to the fact that the item was frozen and later abolished.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: Medicaid Drug Use Review programme — 42 CFR part 456 subpart K (§456.703, §456.705), implementing section 1927(g) of the Social Security Act
rows.basis: Mixed-feed instrument, classified on its dominant arm. Retrospective DUR under §456.705 is defined as ongoing periodic examination of the state's Medicaid claims data and other records, which for a state Medicaid agency includes medical claims carrying ICD-10-CM diagnoses that the state requires for adjudication independent of DUR — hence claims-with-diagnosis, carriesCondition true, and reimbursement-justifying pressure. The prospective arm at point of sale fires on the pharmacy transaction and the drug profile alone, which is dispensing-only; the row therefore understates feed heterogeneity. Criterion shape is 'other' because the regulation mandates a bundle (therapeutic duplication, drug-disease contraindication, drug-drug interaction, incorrect dosage and duration, clinical abuse/misuse) rather than one rule shape. ConditionRole is unknown because the regulation authors no criterion logic of its own — it explicitly delegates the predetermined standards to states, contractors and compendia, so there is no denominator here whose severability I can test. I could not fetch the eCFR text (blocked by redirect), so this rests on the regulation's structure as recorded in the instrument entry plus general knowledge of the programme.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: iPLEDGE REMS for isotretinoin (FDA-mandated Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy; restricted distribution)
rows.basis: The instrument runs on a purpose-built authorization registry: prescribers, pharmacies and patients enrol, negative pregnancy test results and confirmation of contraception are entered into that registry, and dispensing is gated by a registry lookup within a 7-day window rather than by any claims or EHR feed. The registry contains pregnancy status only because this REMS created the requirement, so substrateCarriesCondition is false and coding pressure is none — no payer requires a pregnancy determination for isotretinoin to be paid. Shape is avoidance (absolute contraindication in pregnancy) wrapped in a monitoring apparatus. ConditionRole is load-bearing here rather than severable because the instrument is not a rate: the entire computation performed at dispensing is the pregnancy-status determination, and deleting it leaves no decision to make. Could not fetch an FDA primary page (404 on the URL tried), so this rests on the operational definition recorded in the instrument entry.

rows.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety
rows.instrument: CMS eCQM CMS146v12 'Appropriate Testing for Pharyngitis' (measure steward: NCQA) — used in the Merit-based Incentive Payment System and the Medicaid Child Core Set
rows.basis: Verified against the eCQI Resource Center specification for CMS146: it is an eCQM computed on electronic health record data expressed in QDM 5.6 and reported via QRDA, and the denominator is outpatient/telephone/virtual/ED encounters with a pharyngitis or tonsillitis diagnosis plus an antibiotic order within three days, for patients aged 3+. An EHR carries coded encounter diagnoses for care documentation and for billing the visit, independent of this measure. Criterion shape is monitoring: the numerator event is performance of a group A streptococcus test in a seven-day window around the episode, i.e. a required test accompanying the drug, not an avoidance or dosing rule. ConditionRole is load-bearing because the pharyngitis diagnosis is what defines the episode and selects which test counts; removing it leaves no coherent denominator for the strep-test numerator.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: A250 薬剤総合評価調整加算 + 薬剤調整加算 (Comprehensive Medication Evaluation and Adjustment Addition, inpatient, 100 pts + 150 pts)
rows.basis: The fee is claimed on the inpatient 医科レセプト (DPC/出来高), on which 傷病名 is a mandatory adjudication field, so the feed the instrument fires into carries coded disease names for payment reasons unrelated to polypharmacy. Rule shape is neither undertreatment nor avoidance: it is review-and-deprescribe (patient on >=6 internal medicines at admission, comprehensive evaluation, >=2 fewer at discharge), classified 'other'. Because the trigger is a drug count, deleting any condition axis still leaves a fully computable and payable event, hence severable. Fee-schedule structure from the MHLW 診療報酬点数表 as summarised in the dataset's own binding field (別紙36の2 chlorpromazine-equivalence table); I could not open the primary notification (web search budget exhausted).

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: B008-2 薬剤総合評価調整管理料 (Comprehensive Medication Evaluation and Adjustment Management Fee, outpatient, 250 pts; 連携管理加算 50 pts)
rows.basis: Outpatient 医科レセプト submission, which carries mandatory 傷病名 for adjudication independent of any medication-safety rule. Criterion is a review-and-reduce rule keyed to an oral drug count, so it computes without a condition; condition axis is a refinement. Primary fee notification not reached; classification rests on the fee-schedule structure and on the general architecture of Japanese medical claims.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: 区分14の3 服用薬剤調整支援料1 および 2 (Medication Adjustment Support Fee, community pharmacy, 調剤報酬点数表)
rows.basis: This is a 調剤報酬 fee billed on the pharmacy claim (調剤レセプト). Japanese pharmacy claims and the prescriptions they are built from do not carry 傷病名; the pharmacy holds drug, dose, duration and prescriber only. Coding pressure on the condition exists in the system (mandatory 傷病名 on the physician's medical claim) but that record is not in the pharmacy's feed. Rule is review-and-reduce on a drug count (>=6 internal drugs), so severable. Not verified against the primary 調剤報酬点数表 text.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: レセプト記載要領 (claims-form recording rules) data element for the polypharmacy fees
rows.basis: The instrument is a recording rule for data elements on the medical claim; the same claim record mandatorily carries 傷病名 for adjudication, so the substrate carries conditions for reasons independent of the polypharmacy rule. The element itself (per the dataset's binding field: 842100062 drug count before/after) is drug-count only, so the condition plays no computational role and is severable. Element identifiers taken from the dataset, not independently verified.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: 厚生労働省 高齢者の医薬品適正使用の指針（総論編）as cited by the fee notification
rows.basis: A national guidance document with no computable definition and no data feed of its own; it is applied by a clinician or pharmacist reading the patient's record, so the operative substrate is chart review, where conditions are present in narrative and coded form and are humanly adjudicable. Nothing is computed, so 'load-bearing vs severable' does not arise: marked not-applicable rather than forced. Coding pressure recorded at system level (mandatory 傷病名 on Japanese medical claims), acknowledging that frailty/multimorbidity as such is not a 傷病名.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: NICE NG5 recommendation 1.4.1 (structured medication review targeting)
rows.basis: NG5 is guidance; it names who should be considered for a structured medication review and delegates all operationalisation. No data feed, so substrate is the clinician's read of the record. Not-applicable for conditionRole because no measure is computed. Coding pressure marked reimbursement-justifying because the long-term conditions NG5 points at (and comorbidity counts) are QOF register conditions in English general practice, and QOF register membership carries direct payment; this is a class-level inference, not a statement in NG5.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: NHS England Network Contract DES - Structured Medication Reviews and Medicines Optimisation service specification (priority cohorts)
rows.basis: PCNs identify the priority cohorts from the participating practices' GP clinical systems, which hold SNOMED CT coded problem lists, frailty codes and care-home status; the dataset's own binding note confirms the SMR activity code is SNOMED in NHS Digital business rules. The rule is 'who should receive a review', so the cohort definition IS the denominator and deleting it leaves no eligible population to measure against (a bare SMR count per list size would be a different instrument). Frailty/long-term-condition coding in English general practice is contractually and QOF-payment driven, independent of this rule. Primary service specification not opened.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: IIF indicator SMR-01 (Percentage of patients eligible to receive a Structured Medication Review who received a Structured Medication Review), £12.0m / 53 points
rows.basis: IIF indicators are computed from extracts of participating practices' GP clinical systems (GPES/CQRS), which carry SNOMED-coded conditions; the numerator is a SNOMED activity code recorded in that same record. Denominator is 'patients eligible', i.e. the condition/risk-defined cohort, so the condition axis is load-bearing for this indicator's denominator. Extraction route is a programme-level inference (all IIF indicators run off practice clinical-system extracts), not read off the SMR-01 specification, which I could not open.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: IIF indicators SMR-02A, SMR-02B, SMR-02C, SMR-02D (medicines safety), £0.9m / 4 points each, thresholds fully specified
rows.basis: I could not establish what these four indicators measure; the web search budget for this session was exhausted before the IIF guidance could be retrieved and I will not guess indicator wording. Substrate marked ehr-record only on the programme-level fact that IIF indicators are extracted from practice clinical systems, hence low confidence. criterionShape and conditionRole left unknown rather than inferred from the recorded retention value.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: IIF indicator SMR-03 (DOAC monitoring), £2.9m / 13 points
rows.basis: Shape is given by the indicator's own title: a monitoring rule (patients on a DOAC having the required checks). A monitoring numerator requires recorded test results, which exist only in the GP clinical record, so the feed is the EHR extract and carries coded conditions and labs for reasons unrelated to this rule. The denominator is drug-defined (patients on a DOAC), so the clinical criterion's condition axis (renal impairment, low weight, age) is a refinement and its deletion still leaves a computable monitoring rate. IIF specification not opened.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: IIF indicators RESP-01 and RESP-02 (asthma prescribing) - WITHIN-DOCUMENT CONTROL CASE
rows.basis: Denominator is the QOF asthma register, which lives in the GP clinical system as a SNOMED code cluster and is maintained because QOF pays on register membership, entirely independent of any medicines-safety rule. Because the register is the denominator, deleting the condition leaves no population. criterionShape marked 'other' because the pair mixes an over-prescribing (SABA volume) element with a review element and I could not open the specification to confirm which is which; not forced into avoidance or monitoring.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: NHSBSA Medicines Optimisation Polypharmacy Prescribing Comparators, specification v2.2.0 (May 2026), delivered via ePACT2
rows.basis: ePACT2 is built on NHSBSA prescription processing (dispensing) data linked by NHS number; it holds BNF-coded items, quantities, patient age and NHS number, and no clinical diagnosis field of any kind. The comparators are avoidance-shaped (concurrent counts of anticholinergic/CNS/high-risk medicine groups), so a publishable drug rate survives deletion of any condition axis. Coding pressure marked reimbursement-justifying because the relevant conditions (dementia, falls-risk long-term conditions) are QOF-register coded in the GP record for payment; that record is simply not in this feed.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: Polypharmacy case-finding indicators deployed as Scottish Therapeutics Utility (STU) reports and Right Decision Service (RDS) prescribing alerts, via the EScro specification database
rows.basis: STU runs against the practice's own GP clinical system and reads Read/SNOMED coded problems, repeat prescriptions and numeric laboratory results (the dataset's binding field names lab thresholds and dm+d), so the feed carries conditions and labs for general clinical-record reasons. Most case-finding items are hazard combinations of a drug with a condition or lab value, i.e. avoidance-shaped, so a drug-only rate remains computable and the condition is severable. Coding pressure is clinically-recorded-only because QOF was abolished in Scotland (2016 GP contract settlement), removing the payment link to disease-register coding that England retains.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: Polypharmacy National Therapeutic Indicators (Appendix C, 2026-2029 guidance) - the national benchmarking/measurement set for polypharmacy
rows.basis: The instrument's own data source is the national Prescribing Information System, a dispensed-prescription dataset (drug, quantity, prescriber, CHI, age) with no diagnosis field; PIS can be record-linked to other national datasets but the indicators as published are computed on PIS alone. Comparative prescribing-volume indicators are avoidance-shaped, so a rate survives without any condition. Scottish GP condition coding has no QOF payment attached since 2016.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: National prevalence reporting of case-finding indicators from Prescribing Information System (PIS) data, 2018 guidance Table E1
rows.basis: The instrument names its own substrate: national PIS dispensing data, which carries no diagnosis. Note the informative pairing with the STU deployment of the same indicator family: the identical clinical rules run on a condition-carrying EHR feed in-practice and on a condition-free dispensing feed nationally. Avoidance shape, so the condition is severable from the computed rate.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: Medicare Part D Medication Therapy Management (MTM) targeting criteria, 42 CFR 423.153(d)(2)
rows.basis: The entity applying the criteria is the Part D sponsor, whose own adjudication feed is the prescription drug event record, which carries NDC, quantity, days supply and cost and no diagnosis; standalone PDPs therefore identify the required chronic conditions by drug-fill proxy, the same mechanism CMS documents elsewhere in the Part D measure suite. MA-PD sponsors additionally hold encounter diagnoses, so this is a mixed feed and confidence is held at moderate. Rule shape is 'who is targeted for a comprehensive medication review', i.e. review targeting, classified other; the chronic-disease criterion defines the eligible population, so it is load-bearing for the denominator. Coding pressure is reimbursement-justifying at Medicare level because diagnoses are required to adjudicate Part A/B encounters and drive MA risk adjustment, though not to pay a Part D drug claim.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: CMS Part D Star Ratings measure D11 - MTM Program Completion Rate for CMR
rows.basis: Per the dataset's own binding note, the measure is computed from the contract's Part D reporting-requirements MTM data submission, i.e. plan self-report; that file carries MTM eligibility flags and CMR dates, not diagnoses. The denominator is incorporated by reference to the condition-based targeting criteria at 42 CFR 423.153(d), so the condition axis defines the population even though this instrument never touches it directly. Coding pressure recorded at Medicare level as for the MTM row. I could not open the 2026 technical notes.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: PQA/CMS 'Polypharmacy: Use of Multiple Anticholinergic Medications in Older Adults' (Poly-ACH) and 'Polypharmacy: Use of Multiple CNS-Active Medications in Older Adults' (Poly-CNS)
rows.basis: The measure logic reads Part D prescription drug event records plus Common Medicare Environment enrollment fields (hospice, ESRD), so the computation itself is dispensing-plus-enrollment. substrateCarriesCondition is nonetheless marked true because the computing environment is CMS's own Medicare data, where ICD-10 diagnoses for the same beneficiaries are present from Part A/B claims and encounter data and are used by sibling measures in the identical Patient Safety suite; the feed is therefore condition-capable for reasons wholly independent of this rule. Avoidance shape (concurrent counts of multiple anticholinergic or CNS-active drugs), so a publishable drug rate survives deletion of any condition.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: PQA/CMS 'Use of Opioids from Multiple Providers in Persons Without Cancer' (OMP) - CONTRAST CASE within the same measure suite
rows.basis: Computed over Part D prescription drug events joined to Medicare ICD-10 diagnosis data (FFS claims and encounter data) for the cancer and hospice carve-out. The condition here names a legitimate indication that removes patients from the measured population rather than defining it, which is the exclusion-carveout case: 'multiple prescribers of opioids' remains a computable and publishable rate without it. Cancer diagnoses are coded because oncology encounters cannot be adjudicated without them. Rests on the dataset's binding note plus general knowledge of the PQA/CMS Patient Safety suite; the PQA technical specification is member-restricted and was not read.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: MFDS 「의약품 병용금기 성분 등의 지정에 관한 규정」 (Regulation on Designation of Contraindicated Combination Ingredients etc.) - the binding underpinning HIRA's national DUR prescribing/dispensing alert system
rows.basis: The DUR check fires on the real-time prescribing/dispensing transaction sent to HIRA, which carries patient identifier, ingredient, dose, duration, age, sex and a pregnancy flag; the KCD diagnosis sits on the later 요양급여비용 claim, not in the transaction the alert is computed against. So coding pressure on the condition is strong and reimbursement-driven (KCD is mandatory for benefit adjudication in Korea) while the feed this instrument actually runs on does not carry it. Rule is avoidance-shaped (contraindicated combination), so the drug-drug rate is computable without any condition.

rows.domain: General polypharmacy and medication review indicators that are NOT PIM-list based: structured medication review
rows.instrument: NHIS 다제약물 관리사업 (National Health Insurance Service Polypharmacy Management Programme), hospital model - programme guidance
rows.basis: In the hospital model the multidisciplinary team selects and reviews patients inside the hospital's own record system, which holds KCD-coded diagnoses, medication lists and labs; NHIS claims (also KCD-coded for benefit adjudication) supply the initial polypharmacy identification. conditionRole is left unknown because the programme guidance, as recorded in the dataset, explicitly delegates target-criteria setting to participating hospitals, so no denominator logic is fixed at national level and I refuse to infer one from the recorded retention value. Primary programme guidance not opened.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: Polypharmacy case-finding indicators driving the Scottish Therapeutics Utility (STU) and Right Decision Service (RDS) prescribing decision support — hypoglycaemia indicator: 'Documented dementia (or on donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine or memantine) and HbA1c less than 53 mmol/mol'
rows.basis: STU is a practice-installed tool that queries the GP clinical system record (and RDS alerts fire inside the same record), so the feed is the primary-care EHR, which holds Read/SNOMED diagnoses, repeat prescribing and numeric lab results for ordinary care and register reasons unrelated to this rule. Rule shape is target relaxation in dementia (tight control in a patient who should not be tightly controlled), which I classified as dose-adjustment rather than avoidance; that mapping is my judgement, not the document's wording. Condition role: the case-finding query is the conjunction dementia AND HbA1c<53 — strip dementia and what remains is a well-controlled-diabetes count, not a drug rate, so I coded it load-bearing. Coding pressure: Scottish general practice has no per-encounter or per-drug claim, and QOF was withdrawn in Scotland in 2016, so dementia coding here is clinician-entered; not established from a document this session.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: 'Polypharmacy Indicators' full specification (ISD Scotland / Effective Prescribing and Therapeutics) — three hypoglycaemia case-finding indicators with explicit denominator and numerator definitions
rows.basis: The record's own binding string states the denominators/numerators run over 'GP record diagnosis codes, lab results and repeat-prescribing data', which is a direct data-source statement, and case-finding indicators in the Scottish polypharmacy programme are executed inside practice systems rather than on national dispensing data. Shape and role classified as for the STU indicator above (a hypoglycaemia case-finding query is a conjunction of a risk condition and a low HbA1c / hypoglycaemic-drug exposure). I did not open the full specification this session, so the exact three denominators are not established.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: National Therapeutic Indicator (Public Health Scotland / Scottish Government) titled 'Increase Falls Risk: Sulfonylurea use in frail older adults'
rows.basis: The National Therapeutic Indicators are the national comparative prescribing indicator set computed centrally from the Prescribing Information System, i.e. dispensed-prescription records carrying drug, quantity, prescriber, CHI, age and sex but no diagnosis and no lab value. Frailty therefore has no adjudicable representation in the feed. Rule shape is avoidance (do not give a sulfonylurea to a frail older adult), and deleting 'frail' still leaves a publishable sulfonylurea-items-per-1000 rate with an age denominator, hence severable. Substrate identification rests on my knowledge of the PIS-based NTI publication series, not on a document read this session.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: Quality Prescribing for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Guide for Improvement 2024–2027 (Scottish Government) — diabetes-specific NTI set
rows.basis: Row is explicitly the NTI set inside the quality prescribing guide, and NTIs are the PIS-computed national comparative indicators (same machinery as the falls-risk sulfonylurea NTI), so the feed carries drug and demographics only. Caveat: these Scottish guides carry BOTH an NTI set and separate GP-system case-finding indicators; if any indicator in this set is in fact executed in practice systems the substrate would differ. Shape coded as avoidance because the hypoglycaemia-relevant members of the set are sulfonylurea/insulin-exposure indicators, but the set is mixed (it also contains uptake-style indicators), so the single shape label is approximate.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: NICE indicator IND179 — 'Diabetes: HbA1c 58 mmol/mol' (percentage of patients with diabetes WITHOUT moderate or severe frailty at HbA1c ≤58)
rows.basis: NICE general-practice indicators are specified to be computable from the GP clinical system record via the primary-care extraction used for QOF, so the feed carries SNOMED-coded diagnoses, frailty codes and numeric HbA1c results maintained for ordinary care and register purposes. Shape: numerator is achievement of a glycaemic target, i.e. an undertreatment/control measure, with frailty acting as a denominator exclusion. Role: deleting the frailty exclusion still leaves a publishable 'percentage of diabetes patients at HbA1c ≤58', so severable, even though frailty is what makes the pair a safety instrument. Coding pressure: English general practice is capitated with no per-encounter diagnosis adjudication; frailty codes enter the record through the contractual routine frailty identification duty for over-65s and eFI auto-coding rather than through claim payment, which fits neither enum value cleanly — I coded clinically-recorded-only.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: NICE indicator IND180 — 'Diabetes: HbA1c 75 mmol/mol' (patients WITH moderate or severe frailty, relaxed target)
rows.basis: Same substrate reasoning as IND179 (GP clinical system record, coded frailty and numeric HbA1c). Shape coded dose-adjustment because the clinical rule being operationalised is target relaxation in frailty (an over-treatment guard) rather than pure control attainment; an equally defensible reading is undertreatment with a relaxed threshold, so this label is uncertain. Role: deleting the frailty stratifier leaves a computable and publishable 'percentage at HbA1c ≤75' rate, so severable by the stated test, notwithstanding that frailty is the indicator's whole reason for existing.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) 2025/26 indicators DM020 (17 points) and DM021 (10 points) — frailty-stratified HbA1c targets attached directly to GP payment
rows.basis: QOF is computed by running the NHS England business rules against the practice clinical system and returning aggregates through GPES/CQRS, so the substrate is the primary-care EHR, which holds the SNOMED diabetes register and the frailty refsets plus numeric HbA1c values. Shape: the DM020/DM021 pair implements frailty-stratified target individualisation (DM020 alone would read as undertreatment). Role: each half remains a computable, publishable HbA1c-target rate if the frailty stratifier is removed, hence severable. Coding pressure: frailty coding is driven by the GMS contract identification duty rather than by adjudication of a claim or a drug; note that QOF payment itself now rewards it, but that is this rule, not an independent pressure.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: National Diabetes Audit — Report 1: Care Processes and Treatment Targets (NHS Digital)
rows.basis: NDA is a national clinical audit dataset assembled from automated extracts of GP clinical systems plus specialist diabetes service returns; I classified it as a registry because the computation runs on the audit collection rather than on the live record, but its upstream feed is the coded GP EHR, which does carry diagnoses and results independently of any safety rule. Shape: care processes and treatment-target attainment, i.e. control/undertreatment measurement. Role: NDA publishes target attainment stratified by age band and diabetes type, so a risk-condition stratifier is not needed for a publishable rate. Whether the NDA extract actually transmits frailty codes is not established.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: CMS eCQM CMS122v13 / MIPS Quality ID #001 — 'Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Poor Control (>9%)' (steward NCQA, used in the Medicare Quality Payment Program)
rows.basis: As an eCQM the measure is computed over certified-EHR data exported as QRDA, and the frailty/advanced-illness exclusions are expressed as ICD-10/SNOMED, HCPCS device and CPT encounter value sets — i.e. billing-shaped codes that sit in the record because US encounters, DME supply and facility stays are adjudicated on coded diagnoses and procedures, independent of this measure. Shape: inverse control measure (HbA1c >9% = poor control), so undertreatment. Role: the frailty/advanced-illness exclusion removes patients from the denominator; deleting it still leaves the whole diabetes poor-control rate, so severable. Note the MIPS CQM variant of #001 may run on a different feed; I classified the eCQM named in the row.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: HEDIS 'Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes (GSD)' — advanced illness and frailty exclusion for members aged 66+
rows.basis: HEDIS is computed by health plans over member claims/encounter data (with supplemental clinical and lab feeds for the result value; GSD sits in NCQA's ECDS-style reporting, which blends claims with EHR/lab extracts). Diagnoses are present in that feed because a payer will not adjudicate a claim without them, and the frailty/advanced-illness exclusion value sets are exactly such billed diagnoses, SNF/DME/home-care codes. Shape: glycaemic status/control attainment, i.e. undertreatment framing, with the 66+ frailty and advanced-illness exclusion as an over-treatment guard. Role: deleting the exclusion leaves a publishable plan-level glycaemic control rate, so severable.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: CMS eCQM CMS816v4 — 'Hospital Harm – Severe Hypoglycemia' (CBE 3503e; steward CMS; used in hospital quality reporting)
rows.basis: Substrate is the inpatient certified EHR: the measure pairs administration of an antihyperglycaemic agent with a subsequent laboratory or point-of-care glucose result, and neither the administration timestamp nor the glucose value exists in a claims feed, so it must run on hospital EHR data. That feed also carries coded diagnoses because inpatient stays are billed on them. Shape: this is an adverse-outcome/harm measure rather than an undertreatment, avoidance, dose-adjustment or monitoring rule, so I coded 'other'; a monitoring reading (glucose surveillance after a hypoglycaemic agent) is defensible and I could not confirm the numerator logic against the specification this session. Role: the denominator is drug exposure with no risk condition; a drug-exposure harm rate is publishable without one, so severable.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: HEDIS 'Emergency Department Visits for Hypoglycemia in Older Adults With Diabetes (EDH)' (NCQA)
rows.basis: HEDIS utilisation measures of this kind are computed over plan claims/encounter data; both the denominator (older members with diabetes) and the numerator (ED visits with a hypoglycaemia diagnosis) are claims constructs, and diagnoses are present because claims are adjudicated on them. Shape coded 'other' because the measure counts a harm event rather than stating an undertreatment, avoidance, dose-adjustment or monitoring rule. Role: an ED-visit rate among older diabetes patients is publishable without any hypoglycaemia-risk stratifier (CKD, frailty, dementia), so any such stratifier would be severable. Numerator/denominator details not verified this session.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: PQA / CMS Part D Star Ratings 'Statin Use in Persons with Diabetes (SUPD)' — mechanism illustration: diabetes identified by medication fills because Part D claims carry no diagnoses
rows.basis: The measure is computed by CMS over Part D prescription drug event records, which are pharmacy dispensing transactions carrying NDC, fill date, days supply and cost but no diagnosis field; this is why the denominator condition is built from antidiabetic medication fills rather than from a diagnosis code list. Shape: patients with a condition who are NOT receiving an indicated drug, i.e. a textbook undertreatment rule. Role: the numerator event is the absence of a statin, which has no population without the condition, so the condition is load-bearing and could not be deleted — it was proxied instead. Coding pressure: none in this feed; diabetes is reimbursement-justifying in Part A/B claims, but those are not the data this instrument runs on.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: HIRA 2025년(2주기 3차) 고혈압·당뇨병 적정성평가 — indicator 11 당화혈색소 조절률 (HbA1c control rate), with 가산지급 (incentive payment) attached to grading
rows.basis: HIRA's appropriateness evaluations are computed over the national 요양급여비용 청구자료, which carry KCD diagnosis codes because HIRA will not adjudicate a claim without them (the record itself notes E10–E14 and I10–I13 are authored and applied). Caveat: a control RATE needs the actual HbA1c value, which is not a claims field, so this indicator must draw laboratory results from a supplementary institution-level data submission; I could not confirm that collection route this session. Shape: attainment of a glycaemic target, i.e. undertreatment framing. Role and coding pressure are scored against the safety-relevant axis for this domain, the hypoglycaemia-risk condition (frailty, cognitive impairment, advanced age): that axis is absent, a control rate is publishable without it (severable), and no Korean reimbursement rule forces frailty to be coded (none) — the diabetes indication code, by contrast, is fully reimbursement-justifying.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: 厚生労働省『高齢者の医薬品適正使用の指針（総論編）』 Ｅ．糖尿病治療薬 (MHLW national guidance on appropriate medication use in older adults, diabetes drug section)
rows.basis: This is guidance prose applied by a prescriber to an individual patient; it is not computed over any data feed, so no substrate can be established and substrateCarriesCondition is left null rather than guessed. Shape: the diabetes-drug section pairs relaxed/individualised HbA1c targets by cognitive and ADL status with cautions against sulfonylureas and dose reduction by renal function; I coded dose-adjustment, but the section genuinely mixes dose-adjustment and avoidance. Role: not-applicable, because a guideline has no denominator against which severability can be tested. Coding pressure: Japanese receipts do carry mandatory 傷病名 for adjudication, but the axis this section indexes on (frailty, ADL, cognitive category) is not a reimbursement-coded item, so none.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: G-BA DMP-Anforderungen-Richtlinie, Anlage 1 (DMP Diabetes mellitus Typ 2), §1.3.2.2 'Orientierungsgrößen für die antihyperglykämische Therapie' and §1.7.2.2 — a legally binding federal directive
rows.basis: Legally binding it may be, but this section states therapy orientation values for the treating physician; it is not itself computed over a data feed, so substrate is unknown and substrateCarriesCondition is null.
