Shape: individualised glycaemic orientation values weighing hypoglycaemia risk, age and comorbidity, i.e. dose-adjustment; I could not open the current directive text this session, so the precise wording of §1.3.2.2 and the content of §1.7.2.2 are not established. Role: not-applicable (directive, no denominator). Coding pressure: German ambulatory billing does force ICD-10-GM coding of diagnoses, but there is no coded item for the hypoglycaemia-risk stratum this section turns on, so none — low confidence.

rows.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
rows.instrument: G-BA DMP-A-RL, Anlage 1 §2 Qualitätsziele und Qualitätsindikatoren + Anlage 8 (Diabetes mellitus Typ 1 und Typ 2 – Dokumentation), field 20 'HbA1c-Zielwert'
rows.basis: The quality indicators are computed over the structured eDMP documentation dataset that participating practices submit for each patient at each documentation interval, which is a purpose-built disease-management registry rather than a claims or dispensing feed. That dataset carries structured clinical fields (diabetes type, comorbidities and complications, and hypoglycaemia events) recorded as a condition of DMP participation, independent of this particular target field — hence substrateCarriesCondition true, though I could not open Anlage 8 this session to confirm which fields are present in the current version. Shape: individualised HbA1c target, i.e. dose-adjustment. Role: field 20 is a clinician-declared target-achieved/not-achieved flag, so the risk condition is internalised in clinician judgement and a target-attainment rate is publishable without any coded stratifier (severable). Coding pressure: the diabetes diagnosis is required for DMP enrolment and payment, but the hypoglycaemia-risk axis is not a coded, payer-required item — none.

rows.domain: Renal dose adjustment and drugs contraindicated by kidney function (condition axis = eGFR / CrCl / CKD stage) — element index 2 of instruments_flat.json, 13 instruments
rows.instrument: PINCER national rollout, prescribing safety indicator K: 'Prescription of an oral NSAID to a patient with eGFR <45 mL/min' (PRIMIS, University of Nottingham; rolled out nationally via NHS England / the AHSN-Health Innovation Network)
rows.basis: PRIMIS PINCER Query Library documents read (query overview/analysis document and the national scale-up indicator table): indicator K denominator = 'Patients aged >=18 years with chronic renal failure: eGFR <45 mL/min at least 3 months before the audit date'; numerator = 'Patients prescribed an oral NSAID within the 3 months leading up to the audit date'. The query library is extracted from the practice's own GP clinical system (MIQUEST extraction fields are named explicitly, e.g. 'Latest Renal Function Code 15M-0M | MIQUEST') and results are viewed in CHART. Substrate is therefore the GP EHR, which holds the eGFR as a numeric lab result reported routinely with U&E testing, i.e. for reasons wholly unrelated to this rule. No payer requires an eGFR to be present for the consultation or the NSAID to be reimbursed (English general practice is capitation-funded; NSAIDs carry no prior-authorisation). Deleting the eGFR filter still leaves an NSAID prescribing rate, so the condition is severable; PINCER's own sibling indicators are drug-only pairs, demonstrating that.

rows.domain: Renal dose adjustment and drugs contraindicated by kidney function (condition axis = eGFR / CrCl / CKD stage) — element index 2 of instruments_flat.json, 13 instruments
rows.instrument: NICE indicator IND232 'Kidney conditions: eGFR for long-term NSAID use' (NICE indicator menu; designated 'General practice indicator suitable for use in the Quality and Outcomes Framework')
rows.basis: Primary document read (NICE IND232 PDF, published 24 August 2022, retrieved 2026-09-01). Numerator = 'The number of patients in the denominator who have had an eGFR measurement in the preceding 12 months'; Denominator = 'The number of patients (excluding those on the CKD register) prescribed long-term (chronic) oral NSAIDs', long-term = 12 prescriptions in 24 months; Exclusions: None. It is a general practice indicator, computed from the GP clinical record (SNOMED clusters ORALNSAIDDRUG_COD, CKD_COD, EGFR_COD), which carries both the CKD register codes and eGFR results for ordinary clinical reasons. Shape is monitoring, not avoidance: no eGFR threshold is ever tested, only whether a measurement exists. conditionRole coded load-bearing under the stated definition ('deleting the condition leaves no computable measure') because the kidney axis IS the numerator event — delete it and nothing remains; note the contrary reading, that the CKD-register component is a severable denominator exclusion. Confidence set to moderate for that role ambiguity only; substrate and shape are document-established. codingPressure: CKD register membership does attract QOF reward indirectly, but nothing requires either the CKD code or the eGFR to be recorded for an encounter or for the NSAID to be paid.

rows.instrument: NHS Business Services Authority / NHS Digital 'Medication Safety Indicators Specification' — Acute Kidney Injury indicator AKI01 (national medicines-optimisation dashboard)
rows.basis: Primary document read (NHSBSA/NHS Digital 'Medication Safety Indicators Specification', 2019, 51pp, retrieved and text-extracted 2026-09-01). Data Sources section: NHSBSA prescription processing system, 'all NHS prescriptions dispensed data'; 'Analysis is based on drugs that were reimbursed by the NHSBSA. It excludes items not dispensed and disallowed'; only prescriptions where the NHS number could be captured and PDS-verified. AKI01 increased-risk indicator: numerator = patients prescribed NSAID + RAS drug + diuretic; denominator = patients prescribed NSAID or RAS drug or diuretic; bound by BNF codes only (100101, 0202, 0205051, 0205052). No eGFR, no CKD register, no patient diagnosis anywhere on the prescribing side. The admission-rate variant links to HES Admitted Patient Care by NHS number and applies ICD-10 N170-N179/O904, but those codes are the AKI OUTCOME event, not the index renal condition the clinical criterion is written on. rows.basis: QOF guidance for 2025/26 read (NHS England, PRN01904): a QOF Chronic Kidney Disease Register exists and is used as a denominator component of CHOL003 (statin prescribing across CHD/PAD/stroke-TIA/CKD registers), but the indicator tables contain no CKD clinical domain and no drug-safety indicator conditioned on kidney function. Substrate is well established generically — QOF indicators are computed from the GP clinical system via the business rules and extracted for payment — and the register is a SNOMED code cluster, so the feed does carry the condition. criterionShape coded 'other' because the instrument implements register/case-identification logic rather than an undertreatment, avoidance, dose-adjustment or monitoring drug rule; conditionRole 'not-applicable' for the same reason. rows.instrument: All Wales Therapeutics and Toxicology Centre (AWTTC) National Prescribing Indicators 2025-2026 Specifications / NPIs 2025-2028 — Prescribing Safety Indicators related to AKI and to antimicrobial stewardship
rows.basis: Primary document read (National Prescribing Indicators 2025-2026 Specifications, AWTTC, retrieved 2026-09-01), section 2.1.1 Prescribing Safety Indicators. The specification states 'Data source: DHCW' for these indicators specifically, in contrast to 'Data source: NWSSP' (dispensing/CASPA data) used for every drug-volume NPI in the document — so this instrument alone among the Welsh set runs on the Digital Health and Care Wales GP record extract. Units of measure read CKD register membership (stage 3-5) and numeric eGFR (<59 ml/min; nitrofurantoin <45 ml/min) alongside repeat prescriptions. Both register codes and eGFR sit in the Welsh GP record for clinical reasons; Wales has no QOF and no diagnosis-adjudicated claim, so no payer forces the code. Severability is demonstrated inside the same list: 'Number of patients with concurrent prescriptions of an NSAID, RAS drug and a diuretic' is the identical clinical topic with the condition deleted. One indicator in the bundle ('aged 75+ on ACE inhibitor or loop diuretic without a check of renal function in the previous 15 months') is a monitoring rule in which the axis is load-bearing; the row is coded on the dominant avoidance shape.

rows.instrument: KNMP G-Standaard — 'bewaking op verminderde nierfunctie' (medication surveillance for reduced kidney function), the national drug database delivered into every Dutch pharmacy and GP information system
rows.basis: KNMP announcement of the January 2026 clearance cut-offs (80/50/30/10 -> 90/60/30/15 ml/min) plus the Richtlijnendatabase CNS module read 2026-09-01, which states the surveillance behind the G-Standaard 'is in verschillende softwaresystemen ingebouwd en daarmee toegankelijk in de huisarts- en apotheekinformatiesystemen, maar ook in diverse voorschrijf- en apotheeksystemen in de tweede lijn'. Substrate is therefore the prescribing/dispensing patient record, not a claims or sales feed. substrateCarriesCondition deliberately left null rather than guessed, because it differs by arm and the difference is exactly what the hypothesis turns on: in the huisarts/hospital record the creatinine clearance is present as a routine lab result independent of any rule, whereas in the pharmacy AIS it is present only because the prescriber is required to transmit a known reduced kidney function to the pharmacist — a transmission mandated for medication surveillance, i.e. for this rule. A dose-adjustment alert produces no output at all without the clearance value, hence load-bearing. Dutch dispensing reimbursement requires no diagnosis, so there is no payer pressure on the value.

rows.instrument: Federatie Medisch Specialisten / Richtlijnendatabase, Richtlijn Chronische nierschade (CNS): 'Aanpassing medicatie op grond van nierfunctie'

It is prose guidance that computes nothing itself and authors no binding: 'In algemene zin wordt aangeraden de dosering van de medicatie aan te passen volgens de adviezen in de G-Standaard' and 'Bij patienten met chronische nierschade wordt voor medicatieaanpassingsadviezen bij voorkeur verwezen naar de G-Standaard'. rows.instrument: NCQA HEDIS 'Potentially Harmful Drug-Disease Interactions in Older Adults (DDE)', Rate 3: Chronic Kidney Disease and Cox-2 Selective NSAIDs or Nonaspirin NSAIDs
rows.basis: Primary specification read (NCQA DDE measure PDF, retrieved 2026-09-01). Header is literally 'Administrative Specification'; benefit required = 'Medical and pharmacy'; eligible population = continuously enrolled members 66+. Rate 3 additional eligible population criteria: CKD identified from ESRD Diagnosis Value Set, CKD Stage 4 Value Set, Dialysis Procedure, Total Nephrectomy or Kidney Transplant value sets, each with the instruction 'Do not include laboratory claims (claims with POS code 81)'. Numerator = a dispensed ambulatory prescription for a Cox-2 selective or nonaspirin NSAID. So the substrate is medical + pharmacy claims; the diagnosis is what that feed carries and the lab value is explicitly excluded as unusable. Diagnoses are on those encounter claims because US medical claims are not adjudicated without one, independent of this measure — note however that CKD is a hazard here, not an indication for the NSAID, so the pressure is generic-encounter pressure, not drug-justifying pressure. Deleting CKD still yields a publishable NSAID dispensing rate in 66+.

rows.instrument: HIRA / MFDS 의약품안전사용서비스 (DUR) — the national real-time prescribing and dispensing check system
rows.basis: HIRA DUR page read 2026-09-01. The service is described as providing safety information in real time to the institution at the moment of 처방·조제, and the check returns exactly nine categories: 병용금기, 연령금기, 임부금기, 사용(급여)중지, 동일성분중복, 효능군중복, 용량주의, 투여기간주의, 노인주의. Every one of those is computable from the drug ingredient code (주성분코드) plus patient age/sex and a transmitted pregnancy flag; there is no renal or diagnosis-conditioned category. The DUR transaction is the prescription message, not the claim: it carries no KCD diagnosis and no laboratory result. circularRows: HEDIS HDO/UOD/COU (NCQA) — THE ONE FATAL CASE. The row is graded "high", and the notes state the grading rule explicitly: "nothing is marked high unless the substrate is structurally forced (HEDIS exclusion value sets can only be evaluated against medical claims)." That is the circular form verbatim: the instrument binds three diagnosis value sets, therefore the feed must carry diagnoses. The value-set binding IS retained=true. Strip that sentence and what remains is the generic claim that HEDIS runs on plan administrative data — true and independent, but it establishes only that a claims warehouse EXISTS, not that this measure is computed over the medical-claims half of it rather than the pharmacy-claims half. Downgrade to moderate.

Medicare Part C & D Star Ratings OHD/OMP/OHDMP — PARTIALLY CIRCULAR AND UNVERIFIED. The binding field says outright "not verified — PQA technical specifications are member-restricted," and the row still asserts substrateCarriesCondition=true. The evidence chain runs: the measure name says "in Persons Without Cancer" → a cancer exclusion must be evaluated → CMS holds FFS claims and MA Encounter Data → therefore diagnoses. Step one is the outcome. The independent residue (CMS holds PDE + FFS + EDS) is real but proves capability, not use: a PQA cancer exclusion can equally be implemented off antineoplastic NDCs or hospice enrollment flags, both of which live in the drug/enrollment feed and would make the substrate call false. Nobody read the spec. Downgrade to low.

The row concedes "I could not open the MFDS standard or the NIMS reporting schema this session to confirm the exact fields transmitted." What is left is a belief about NIMS field structure plus one observation: "no KCD binding anywhere." That observation is retained=false restated. An unverified architectural assumption plus the outcome variable is not an independent substrate determination. Downgrade to low. (The call may well be right — 사전알리미 does run on 마약류통합관리시스템 rather than HIRA claims — but this record does not establish it.)

The substrate call itself is clean: "an eCQM is by construction computed over the hospital's certified EHR and reported as QRDA" is a fact about the reporting programme that holds whatever this measure binds. countryInferredRows: Medicare Part C & D Star Ratings OHD/OMP/OHDMP — substrate inferred from PAYER architecture ("CMS holds PDE, FFS claims and EDS") rather than from the measure's own computation path, with the spec admittedly unread. This is the precise hazard the task warns about, and this domain proves it: three US rows sit on three different substrates (HEDIS claims-with-diagnosis, Part D POS dispensing-only, Star Ratings claims-with-diagnosis). "CMS has diagnoses somewhere" is compatible with a measure that never touches them. Not acceptable as stated.

MFDS 사전알리미 (Republic of Korea) — substrate inferred from national system architecture, unverified. Korea runs opioid-relevant instruments on at least two structurally different feeds: HIRA 요양급여 claims (carry KCD 상병 because the payer will not adjudicate without one) and MFDS 마약류통합관리시스템 (a Narcotics Control Act custody feed). The row picks NIMS, which is probably correct, but on an assumption it could not check. A single Korean row assigned to the wrong feed flips the sign of this domain's contribution to H-SUBSTRATE, because it is one of only two retained=false rows here.

NOT flagged, for the record: the England NHSBSA row and the eCQM row both name a specific data pipeline (ePACT2 dispensed-prescription data; certified EHR → QRDA) whose diagnosis-carrying status is fixed by the pipeline's design and not by anything either instrument does. England also runs QOF over EHR extracts, and the row explicitly refuses that inference ("whatever the GP record holds"). These are programme-level, not country-level, and they are the two cleanest rows in the set.
shapeErrors: NUMERATOR-DIRECTION CHECK (task 3): all six criterionShape=avoidance calls survive. Numerator events are, in order: an opioid dispensing at high dose that happened; a discharge prescription pair that happened; a POS transaction that happened; a high-dose/multi-provider dispensing that happened; an opioid item dispensed; a prescription exceeding a ceiling. Every one is a prescription that OCCURRED. There is no rule anywhere in this domain whose numerator is a drug ABSENCE, so no undertreatment rule has been misfiled as avoidance and no percentage-form confusion is present.

UNIT-OF-ANALYSIS ERROR, Part D POS edits: one row bundles four rules of three different shapes — a 7-day opioid-naive duration ceiling, a 90 MME soft care-coordination trigger (monitoring, as the notes concede), a drug-drug avoidance edit, and a duplicative-LA-therapy check. Every other row in the domain is a single named measure. Bundling makes this row non-comparable, and it is the single most consequential row in the domain (the only substrate/retention disagreement), so its shape must not be a summary. Split per edit or record shape as mixed.

conditionRole IS CODED OFF TWO DIFFERENT OBJECTS. For rows 1–4 (retained=true) the role is read off the instrument's actual exclusion value sets. For rows 5–6 (retained=false) there are no exclusions in the instrument at all, so the role is read off the underlying CLINICAL criterion. That means conditionRole is populated from the instrument when the outcome is true and from the source criterion when the outcome is false — the coding procedure itself is conditioned on the outcome. Even with correct values this is an outcome-aware pipeline and must be redefined to read off the source criterion for ALL rows.

codingPressure IS PERFECTLY COLLINEAR WITH substrateCarriesCondition ACROSS ALL SIX ROWS (true↔reimbursement-justifying in rows 1,2,4; false↔none in rows 3,5,6, phi = 1.0). It was therefore not independently observed — it was derived, and rows 5–6 say so in as many words ("no condition-coding pressure exists in the dispensing feed"). H-SUBSTRATE and H-CODING-PRESSURE cannot be separated in this domain, and pooling these rows will double-count one measurement as two converging confirmations. H-CODING-PRESSURE needs its discriminating cases: rows where the feed carries conditions but the specific condition is a hazard with no reimbursement pressure behind it. This domain contains none.

conditionRole HAS ZERO VARIANCE (six exclusion-carveouts), which the record itself flags — correctly, and the recommendation to stratify severability by domain should be adopted. But the notes understate it: the record also says exclusion-carveout and severable-refinement "both technically apply" and were separated by convention. A category boundary that is settled by convention rather than by observation cannot bear a hypothesis test; H-SEVERABILITY needs an operational rule (is the condition in the DENOMINATOR definition? — yes for undertreatment, no for carve-outs) applied blind.

DEPENDENT-VARIABLE ERROR, Part D POS edits: retained=true with binding "NONE authored by CMS — explicitly delegated to Part D sponsors and pharmacist judgment." The outcome is defined as the condition axis surviving into the instrument's COMPUTABLE definition. A carve-out written in prose and resolved by a pharmacist at the counter is not computable. This row looks like it should be retained=false, and it is the sole row in the domain that disconfirms H-SUBSTRATE. Fixing it would take the domain from 5/6 to 6/6 agreement — which is exactly why an outcome coder, not a hypothesis-holding analyst, must adjudicate it. Refer upstream; do not fix it inside this classification.

OUTCOME AWARENESS IS DISCLOSED, NOT ABSENT. The notes assert "I did not use the retained field in reaching any classification," then supply a bespoke reconciling story for the one row where substrate and retention disagree ("CMS wrote the carve-out in prose and pushed the determination onto the pharmacist"). Generating a rescue for the single disconfirming case requires having looked at the outcome for that case. The disclosure is honest and the story is probably true, but the claim of blindness does not hold and should not be repeated in the writeup.

UNIT MISMATCH, MFDS row: 사전알리미 produces a prescriber-level exceedance notification, not a patient-level rate. Every other row yields a population rate. This affects what "deleting the condition still yields a publishable rate" means for the severability test and should be recorded rather than assimilated.

circularRows: Row 1 - Northern Ireland, QOF AF v34.0NI (AF001/AF006/AF007): CIRCULAR. The entire evidence for substrate=ehr-record / substrateCarriesCondition=true is that the indicator binds to Read v2/CTV3 clusters (AFIB_COD, CHADVASC_COD). The indicator using diagnosis clusters IS the retention outcome, not evidence about the feed. The one independence claim added ('carries CHA2DS2-VASc values as ordinary general-practice recording, not for this rule') is affirmatively false: CHA2DS2-VASc is recorded in UK GP records largely BECAUSE AF006 pays for recording it, so the risk-stratum axis is caused by the instrument family, not independent of it. Confidence 'high' is unsupportable.

Row 2 - England, NHS England QOF AF001/AF006/AF007/AF008: CIRCULAR, same form. 'Binding is SNOMED refsets published by the Primary Care Domain and executed against the GP record; the GP record carries coded diagnoses and CHA2DS2-VASc values independently of this rule' - the first clause is the outcome, the second is bare assertion. Nothing in the basis observes the feed independently of the indicator (no GPES/CQRS extract spec, no evidence of AF or CHADVASC coding density outside QOF). Confidence 'high' is unsupportable.

Row 3 - Scotland, Polypharmacy Appendix D / STU case-finding: CIRCULAR in the weakest possible form. The EScro specification was never opened. The conclusion may well be right (STU is a practice-installed tool), but the stated basis does not establish it.

Row 5 - United States, MIPS Quality ID #326 v10.0: CIRCULAR AND country-inferred. 'The stated binding is an ICD-10-CM denominator diagnosis list plus HCPCS G-codes; both are billing-data constructs' - the measure's use of ICD-10 is the outcome. The row then concedes it could not confirm which collection type is authoritative, which is the decisive fact for substrate: MIPS CQM #326 is a registry/EHR-abstracted collection type, not necessarily a Part B claims measure.
countryInferredRows: Row 5 - United States: substrate=claims-with-diagnosis and codingPressure=reimbursement-justifying both rest on national facts ('a US professional claim will not adjudicate without a diagnosis', 'nonvalvular AF is an HCC'), not on #326's own data source. Country-level claims-system fact overrides the instrument's own stated data source.

Mixed levels of analysis inside one row.

Defensible as background, but it is a country-level inference and is applied asymmetrically (see shapeErrors).
Row 2 - England: same country-level codingPressure inference, same asymmetry.
Row 3 - Scotland: same country-level codingPressure inference; also the substrate call is generic-UK-GP reasoning rather than anything read out of the EScro spec.
shapeErrors: criterionShape was assigned from the clinical INTENT of the criterion, not from the instrument's numerator, in all seven rows. Applying the numerator test: AF007/AF008 (percentage of AF patients at risk WHO ARE currently treated), MIPS #326 (percentage prescribed), STR0020/STR0021 (퇴원처방률 = discharge prescription RATE), and the Scottish NTI (dispensed volume) all have a numerator event that is a prescription that HAPPENED. These are coverage/compliance rates, not absence-numerator rules. Only Row 3 (STU case-finding: 'AF and no anticoagulant', which outputs a patient list) has a numerator that is a prescription that did NOT happen.

Consequently the note's headline claim - 'criterionShape is undertreatment for all seven rows and the domain carries no within-domain variation on H-SEVERABILITY' - is false. Once the numerator test is applied there is a 6-to-1 split, and the single dissenting row is the decision-support instrument. The element was reported as contributing a constant when it actually contributes the only kind of variation H-SEVERABILITY needs.

The conditionRole assignments across the element rest on an argument that is false for six of the seven instruments. 'The numerator is an absence and absence has no population' cannot justify load-bearing-denominator for a rate whose numerator is a drug present. Deleting AF from 'percentage of AF patients on an anticoagulant' leaves 'percentage of registered patients on an anticoagulant' - publishable, and the Scottish NTI publishes exactly that. The classifier noticed this conflict, stated it, and then resolved it in the direction H-SEVERABILITY prefers. A classifier told to classify on observable properties must take the operational test (does a publishable drug rate survive deletion?) over the hypothesis's narrative reading.

Row 4 unit-of-analysis error, self-declared: criterionShape and conditionRole 'are recorded for the underlying clinical criterion, not the arithmetic this instrument actually publishes'. The classification unit is the instrument's computable definition. An instrument whose computable definition contains no condition at all cannot have a load-bearing condition; recording one there manufactures a counterexample rather than observing one.

Rows 6 and 7 switch the condition axis mid-domain on an identical feed. Row 6 evaluates carriage of atrial fibrillation and returns false; Row 7 silently substitutes ischaemic stroke as 'the condition this instrument actually uses' and returns true. Row 7 is explicitly labelled 'the sibling indicator WITHOUT the AF condition' - the instrument that dropped the axis. Re-defining the axis to whatever the surviving instrument still carries makes substrateCarriesCondition unfalsifiable. The axis must be held fixed per domain (AF), which makes Row 7 false on the same feed as Row 6.

Row 5 conflates two payment mechanisms. HCC risk adjustment and encounter adjudication force the DIAGNOSIS to be coded; H-CODING-PRESSURE's 'reimbursement-justifying' category is defined as a condition that justifies reimbursement for THE DRUG. US anticoagulants are not indication-adjudicated at the point of dispensing, so the cited mechanism does not support the assigned value.

Asymmetric application of the 'independent of this safety rule' clause in Rows 1-3. QOF register payment is excluded as coding pressure because AF001 sits inside the same instrument family - correct - but the QOF-driven CHA2DS2-VASc value is simultaneously counted as evidence that the substrate carries the condition independently. The same clause must cut both ways: if QOF is not independent pressure, then QOF-induced coding is not independent carriage.

Element-wide confidence inflation. The note concedes that the web-search budget was exhausted before ANY primary specification was opened, and that four specific documents (EScro, MIPS #326 v10.0, HIRA 2020 상세설명서, QOF NI v34.0NI extract mechanics) were unreachable. Under those conditions no row in this element can carry confidence 'high'; two do.
Row 3 carries a stray 'confidenceNote': null key. Minor schema noncompliance, but it indicates the row object was hand-edited after generation, which is worth knowing when the element is re-run.

corrections.why: The row concedes it could not verify field-level provenance of the claims-frame / abstraction split, and its central assignment depended on a condition-axis substitution rather than on the instrument's definition.

H-SUBSTRATE requires the condition in CODED form for a reason independent of the rule; grading a narrative chart as substrate-positive is the definition being bent toward the outcome, and this is precisely a row where the condition was retained.

South Korea — HIRA 요양병원 입원급여 적정성평가 '항정신성의약품 처방률': the argument is the country-level one ('HIRA will not adjudicate a claim without KCD 주상병/부상병'). Neither the original analyst nor this auditor obtained the NHS England Primary Care Dementia Data specification, so the extract's actual fields (and whether the antipsychotic side comes from the same extract or from prescribing data) are unestablished; the row is a country-level generalization about English primary care.
shapeErrors: No avoidance/undertreatment confusion exists in this domain: every real instrument's numerator event is a prescription that HAPPENED (residents who received an antipsychotic), so 'avoidance' is correct wherever an instrument exists. The shape errors here are of a different kind — shapes asserted for rules that have no condition axis, or for objects that publish no rate.

United States — Medicare Part D Star Ratings measure set: criterionShape 'avoidance' is asserted for a measure that is absent from the set. There is no numerator to inspect, so the shape is a property of the clinical criterion, not of any instrument. Should be not-applicable, and the whole row should be excluded from arithmetic rather than counted as a substrate-negative case.

United States — 42 CFR 483.45(e) / F758: an enforcement standard with no numerator, no denominator and no published rate. 'Avoidance' is applied by analogy to the clinical rule. It is also compound: the tag bundles the documented-indication requirement with the gradual-dose-reduction requirement, which is a different shape. The severability test the coding depends on ('deleting the condition still leaves a publishable drug rate') is explicitly conceded not to apply.

Scotland — PHS NTIs: one row bundles structurally different indicators. NTI 8e/8ea and CHNTI 8ea are avoidance rules whose condition axis was replaced by an age threshold; NTI 8pf / CHNTI 8pf ('antipsychotic in combination with two other drugs of dependence') is a concurrent-drug-count rule with no condition term — the same shape the analyst correctly coded 'other' for Japan. Coding both as 'avoidance' is inconsistent with the Japan row and should be split.
Japan — 向精神薬多剤投与減算: shape 'other' is correct, but the conditionRole is not. A rule with no condition term cannot have a severable condition refinement; see corrections.

corrections.instrument: United States — CMS MDS 3.0 QM N047.01 (CMIT 526), QM User's Manual V18.0
corrections.why: The row's own basis concedes the substrate is genuinely hybrid (MDS assessment for drug + three carve-out items; an ICD-10-CM exclusion list read from Medicare/Medicaid claims added at V18.0) and that 'it is not established which side dominates'. A single-value enum picked without that being settled is a low-confidence call. Separately, this row cannot serve as clean evidence for H-SUBSTRATE in either direction: the analyst's own note records that schizophrenia coding in MDS Section I responded to the existence of the measure, which is coding pressure created BY the rule — the exact dependence H-SUBSTRATE requires to be absent.

corrections.instrument: United States — CMS Part D Patient Safety measures DMD08 / DMD09 (PQA APD, APD-LTNH)
corrections.why: Misapplication of the hypothesis's own definition. H-CODING-PRESSURE means the condition justifies reimbursement for THE DRUG IN QUESTION; dementia is the index/hazard condition and justifies payment for no antipsychotic. The stated ground — 'a diagnosis is required for the encounter to adjudicate' — is a property of the FEED, already captured by substrateCarriesCondition=true, and coding it again here double-counts. If every claims-based row is scored reimbursement-justifying on that ground, H-CODING-PRESSURE becomes untestable (claims rows retain by construction). The exclusion-carveout axis on this same measure (approved-indication antipsychotic use) is the axis that would legitimately be reimbursement-justifying, and it is the axis this row does not code.

corrections.instrument: United States — CMS Part D Patient Safety measures DMD08 / DMD09 (PQA APD, APD-LTNH)
corrections.to: split row: severable-refinement (dementia index condition, denominator) + exclusion-carveout (approved-indication antipsychotic use, MAJOR_DEPRESSION)
corrections.why: The basis admits the row 'compresses two structurally different roles into the dominant one'. Under H-SEVERABILITY and H-CODING-PRESSURE those two axes have OPPOSITE predicted behaviour, so collapsing them destroys the discriminating information the domain was scanned for. Per-axis coding is required or this row must be excluded from the severability arithmetic.

corrections.instrument: United States — Medicare Part D Star Ratings measure set (measure absent)
corrections.to: EXCLUDE from all arithmetic; substrate=not-established, criterionShape=not-applicable
corrections.why: Negative space. There is no computable definition, therefore no observable substrate, shape or condition role. As coded it silently enters the tally as a substrate-negative / condition-dropped case and inflates support for H-SUBSTRATE with a row that contains no observation. The analyst flagged this in notes but still emitted classified values; the values must be nulled, not merely caveated.

corrections.instrument: United States — 42 CFR 483.45(e), survey tag F758
corrections.to: false (narrative-only — recommend a distinct enum value, e.g. 'carries-condition-narrative-not-coded')
corrections.why: H-SUBSTRATE is stated as 'already carries the condition IN CODED FORM'. A surveyor reading free-text chart documentation is not a coded feed and there is no value set. Grading it true imports a looser definition on exactly the rows that retained the condition, which manufactures agreement between substrate and retention. If narrative substrates are to count as positive, that must be a declared, pre-registered definitional choice applied uniformly, not a per-row judgement.

corrections.instrument: United States — 42 CFR 483.45(e), survey tag F758
corrections.why: No electronic feed, no value set, no rate; the criterionShape is assigned by analogy and the severability test is conceded not to apply. Every structural property of this row is inferred from regulation text rather than from a computable definition.

corrections.instrument: England — NICE indicator IND12, 'Dementia: anti-psychotic prescriptions'

corrections.instrument: Scotland — PHS National Therapeutic Indicators (NTI 8e/8ea, CHNTI 8ea, NTI 8pf/CHNTI 8pf)
corrections.why: The only 'high' in the domain, and half its basis is circular (the binding's use of an age threshold is the retention outcome, not evidence about the feed). The care-home indicators additionally require a residency flag that a dispensed-prescription feed does not itself carry, so 'dispensing-only' understates a linked substrate. The substrate label is probably right; the confidence level is not earned by the evidence actually adduced.

corrections.instrument: Scotland — PHS National Therapeutic Indicators (NTI 8e/8ea, CHNTI 8ea, NTI 8pf/CHNTI 8pf)

corrections.instrument: South Korea — HIRA 요양병원 입원급여 적정성평가 '항정신성의약품 처방률' (2주기6차)

Scoring it again as drug-specific reimbursement pressure inflates H-CODING-PRESSURE with the same fact counted twice.

corrections.instrument: South Korea — HIRA 요양병원 입원급여 적정성평가 '항정신성의약품 처방률' (2주기6차)
corrections.why: Substrate was established from national claims-system generalities, not from the 세부추진계획's 산출식. HIRA's 요양병원 evaluation ingests 환자평가표 submissions alongside 청구자료, so the feed is hybrid registry/claims and the single value was not adjudicated against a read specification.

corrections.instrument: Japan — MHLW 診療報酬 向精神薬多剤投与 減算 (別紙様式40)
corrections.why: The analyst states plainly that the criterion has no condition term at all. A refinement cannot be severed from a rule that never contained it; 'severable-refinement' here records a deletion that never occurred and would count as evidence for H-SEVERABILITY where there is none. With no condition axis, codingPressure should likewise be not-applicable rather than 'reimbursement-justifying', and the row should be excluded from any condition-axis arithmetic (retain it only in the shape tally).

corrections.instrument: Australia — National Aged Care Mandatory QI Program, 'Medication management - antipsychotics'
corrections.to: false (narrative-only — same recommended distinct value as F758)
corrections.why: Provider free-text clinical records are not a coded feed, and the onward feed to the department/AIHW is aggregate self-report carrying no patient-level condition at all. Whichever of the two stages is chosen as the substrate, neither carries the condition in coded form. Coding true on a row that retained the condition, with the QI Program Manual unread, is back-fill from the outcome.

audits.domain: Paediatric and pregnancy medication safety (domain index 6)
circularRows: England (UK) — NHSBSA Valproate Safety Dashboard (VPA1–VPA5) [confidence: high]: half the substrate basis is 'the stated binding is BNF presentation codes plus PDS sex and age'. That IS the retention outcome. The only non-circular leg is the platform identity (ePACT2/Catalyst = dispensed-prescription warehouse), and the analyst concedes the VPA specification was never opened. The instrument's own quoted sentence ('such patients cannot be identified from the prescribing data used to populate this dashboard', recorded in the source scan) is the genuinely independent evidence and it is not cited in the basis.

England (UK) — NHSBSA Antimicrobial Stewardship Dashboard – Children (ASC01–ASC05): the most nakedly circular row in the set. The basis says the binding 'is BNF drug groupings plus age bands, which is the signature of a dispensing feed with a demographic join and no clinical field'. The absence of a condition binding is the outcome; it is being used as the diagnostic sign of the substrate. The remaining leg is sibling inference from the valproate dashboard, itself unverified.

Republic of Korea — MFDS/KIDS 임부금기 via national DUR: circular AND factually wrong. The basis reasons that the DUR transaction carries no diagnosis because the rule uses a prescriber-entered 임부여부 flag ('The instrument's own binding confirms this shape'). The source scan records the opposite from the primary document: HIRA transmits 질병분류기호 / 주상병코드 AND 임부여부 in the DUR message, returns the diagnosis as display text, and the grading text itself turns on 상병 ('상병에 따라 처방의사가 … 판단'). The feed carries a coded diagnosis field and the rule declines to use it. Coding this row dispensing-only/false converts a documented counterexample to H-SUBSTRATE into a clean confirmation.

Republic of Korea — MFDS/KIDS 특정연령대금기 via national DUR: same circular move, same factual error ('Same DUR prescription-transaction substrate as 임부금기: fires on the transmitted prescription line, no diagnosis present'), plus 'The stated binding is ingredient name plus an age threshold' offered as substrate evidence.

Japan — 小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算: 'the instrument's own binding note says exactly that (prose disease names in the fee notice, adjudicated against the standard 傷病名 master)' cites the instrument's binding as proof of the feed. There is an independent leg here (傷病名 is mandatory on every レセプト for payment, regardless of this add-on), so the substrate value survives; the cited sentence does not support it.

United States (federal) — CMS eCQM CMS146v12 [confidence: high]: the basis establishes the substrate largely from the measure's own denominator ('the denominator is … encounters with a pharyngitis or tonsillitis diagnosis'), which is the retention outcome. The independent leg ('an EHR carries coded encounter diagnoses for care documentation and for billing the visit') is a generic claim about EHRs, not a property of the certified-EHR feed this measure runs on, and is not sourced.

United States (federal) — Medicaid DUR, 42 CFR part 456 subpart K: partly circular by arm selection. The row admits the programme is mixed-feed and then picks the arm (retrospective claims review) that matches the retained-condition outcome, while the condition axis that was actually scored as retained — the mandated drug-disease contraindication screen under §1927(g)(2)(A) — is a point-of-sale prospective screen running on the pharmacy transaction, which the row's own text calls dispensing-only.
countryInferredRows: Republic of Korea — 임부금기: substrate derived from a general architectural claim about how Korean DUR relates to 요양급여 claims ('the KCD diagnosis lives on the 요양급여 claim, which is a separate, later submission'), not from the DUR message specification. The system-level inference is contradicted by the primary-document record in the source scan.
Republic of Korea — 특정연령대금기: substrate asserted as 'Same DUR prescription-transaction substrate as 임부금기' — inherited from a sibling row, which itself inherited from a system-level assumption.

Japan — 妊婦加算: substrate 'claims-with-diagnosis' asserted purely from the fact that Japanese fee-schedule items are billed on レセプト. That is a national-system property, not a determination about this item's feed; the row then concedes it cannot say whether pregnancy is present in that feed at all.

England (UK) — NHSBSA Antimicrobial Stewardship Dashboard – Children: substrate inherited from platform family ('Same NHSBSA prescribing-data platform family as the valproate dashboard'), not read from the ASC01–ASC05 comparator definitions.

United States (federal) — Medicaid DUR: substrate inferred from what a state Medicaid agency's data holdings generally contain ('which for a state Medicaid agency includes medical claims carrying ICD-10-CM diagnoses'), not from the feed the mandated screens actually execute against. §456.703 delegates the standards to states, contractors and compendia, so there is no single national feed to infer.

Wales (UK) — All Wales NPI: NOT country-inferred. This row correctly refuses to resolve the feed and marks substrate unknown. It is the only row in the set whose substrate handling is epistemically clean.
shapeErrors: Japan — 小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算, coded criterionShape 'avoidance': wrong on the stated test. The billable event is '抗菌薬の投与の必要性が認められないため抗菌薬を使用しない' — the numerator is a prescription that DID NOT happen. An absence has no population, so the condition set (急性気道感染症/急性中耳炎/急性副鼻腔炎/急性下痢症, 基礎疾患のない患者, influenza/COVID-19 exclusions, age) is load-bearing, not severable. Structurally identical to an undertreatment rule; only the valence differs. Should be criterionShape 'undertreatment', conditionRole 'load-bearing-denominator'.

Severability test applied inconsistently across the set: literally for the Japanese add-on ('a payable-but-meaningless add-on remains, so severable') and in spirit for iPLEDGE ('nothing remains to compute, so load-bearing'). The two calls point in opposite directions on structurally similar non-rate instruments. Applying the absence-numerator test uniformly fixes both and removes the analyst's own 'least stable calls' concern.

Japan — 妊婦加算: internally inconsistent row. substrate is set to 'claims-with-diagnosis' — an enum value that asserts the feed carries diagnoses — while substrateCarriesCondition is set to null on the ground that it may not. The row asserts in one field what it declines to assert in the next. Substrate should be 'unknown'.

Republic of Korea — 특정연령대금기: conditionRole 'not-applicable' is correct (chronological age is a demographic attribute, not a condition), and therefore this row has no condition axis to retain or drop. It must be REMOVED from the retention denominator, not carried as a drop. The analyst says this in the notes and then leaves the row in the table; the recommendation needs to be operative or it will silently inflate the drop count.

Wales (UK) — All Wales NPI: a single row aggregates a multi-indicator, multi-feed programme, and then assigns one criterionShape ('avoidance') on the strength of subject matter while declaring substrate unknowable without the same unread specification. The epistemics are inconsistent — either the 2025–2028 spec is available for shape or it is not. criterionShape should be 'unknown', or the row should be split per indicator.

United States (federal) — Medicaid DUR: one row is forced to carry two feeds whose retention behaviour differs. The regulation's condition axis (drug-disease contraindication) is mandated on the prospective point-of-sale arm; the coded substrate describes the retrospective arm. Split the row or code substrate 'unknown'.

codingPressure in this element is not measuring what H-CODING-PRESSURE defines. All four 'reimbursement-justifying' codings (HIRA 적정성평가, Japan add-on, Medicaid DUR, CMS146v12) rest on encounter-level adjudication pressure (a 상병코드/傷病名/encounter diagnosis is required for the VISIT to be paid), not on a condition that justifies reimbursement for the drug under scrutiny. The analyst states this in the notes and codes the opposite in the field. Every condition in this domain is a hazard/index condition, so the correct reading is zero variation on this variable — these rows must not be pooled with elements where indication-level carve-outs exist.

substrateCarriesCondition is specified as a property of the feed but is really a property of the (feed, condition) pair. 妊婦加算 exposes it from one side (dense coded feed, specific condition probably absent) and Korean DUR from the other (coded diagnosis field present, the rule's specific condition not derivable from it). Until the field is split, no row in this element should be scored 'true' on the strength of the feed being diagnosis-bearing in general.

Structural note carried from the source scan, not a criterionShape error but affects the arithmetic: iPLEDGE is coded at layer 'payment' in the underlying instrument table. It is a restricted-distribution gate with no payment consequence. If the layer variable is re-used anywhere, that assignment is wrong.

corrections.why: The defining document (VPA1–VPA5 specification) was never opened, and half the stated basis is the instrument's binding, which is the outcome. The substrate value (dispensing-only) is probably right — ePACT2/Catalyst are documented dispensed-prescription warehouses independent of this dashboard, and NHSBSA's own published sentence that hysterectomy patients 'cannot be identified from the prescribing data used to populate this dashboard' is a statement about the feed rather than the rule. Keep the value, re-ground the basis on those two facts, and drop the binding clause.

corrections.why: Substrate rests entirely on (a) sibling inference from another unverified row and (b) the absence of a condition binding, which is the outcome. Nothing independent of the retention outcome establishes the feed for this specific dashboard. criterionShape is separately self-declared as inferred from subject matter.

corrections.instrument: Wales (UK) — All Wales National Prescribing Indicators 2025–2028
corrections.why: The row cannot read the 2025–2028 specification for substrate but assigns a shape to a whole multi-indicator programme from subject matter. Either resolve per indicator or leave shape unknown. The substrate/codingPressure handling on this row is correct and should be the model for the rest of the set.

corrections.instrument: Republic of Korea — MFDS/KIDS 임부금기 via the national DUR system
corrections.to: unknown (documented as a prescription transaction that DOES carry a transmitted diagnosis field, 질병분류기호/주상병코드; no enum value fits — it is emphatically not dispensing-only)

corrections.why: Substrate survives the circularity test cleanly — the 청구명세서 requires 상병코드 for adjudication regardless of any appropriateness indicator, which is independent of the outcome, so this is the one high-confidence substrate call in the element I would let stand. The downgrade is for the row as a whole: the 지표정의서 was not read (the source scan lists it as unverified), so the denominator definition and the severability call rest on the 2023 results report, and codingPressure is now unknown.

corrections.instrument: Japan — 小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 / 耳鼻咽喉科小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算
corrections.why: Apply the numerator test as specified. The add-on is payable precisely when an antibiotic was NOT prescribed. corrections.instrument: Japan — 小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 / 耳鼻咽喉科小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算
corrections.why: Follows directly from the corrected shape. Delete the indication set and there is no event to count: 'a consultation at which no antibiotic was given' is not computable over any population. The row's own hedge ('stripping the condition would leave a payable-but-meaningless add-on') is the definition of load-bearing, not of severable. Note this correction cuts AGAINST tidy arithmetic for H-SEVERABILITY-versus-payment-layer framing and in favour of H-SEVERABILITY itself; it is made on the stated test, not on the direction of the result.

corrections.instrument: Japan — 小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算 / 耳鼻咽喉科小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算
corrections.why: Same defect as the HIRA row: 傷病名 is mandatory for the receipt to be paid, which is encounter-level pressure. No payer requires 急性気道感染症 to be coded in order to reimburse a drug — the fee pays for withholding the drug.

corrections.instrument: Japan — 妊婦加算 (pregnancy consultation add-on)
corrections.why: The enum value 'claims-with-diagnosis' asserts the property the row simultaneously refuses to assert by setting substrateCarriesCondition null. The determination is also national-system-level (Japanese fee items are billed on レセプト) rather than instrument-level, and normal pregnancy sits outside insured care so the specific condition may be absent from an otherwise diagnosis-dense feed. Keep substrateCarriesCondition null and codingPressure unknown; those calls are correct.

circularRows: HEADLINE — substrateCarriesCondition and conditionAxisRetained agree on 17/17 rows (phi = 1.00, zero discordant cells). row 2 — Korea 등급 공개 [HIGH] — CIRCULAR BY INHERITANCE. 'Same KCD binding inherited per the record.' Inherits row 1's contaminated substrate leg; a derivative layer cannot carry more confidence than its parent.

row 3 — Korea 가감지급사업 P4P [HIGH] — CIRCULAR BY INHERITANCE, same as row 2. Note this row is the single most load-bearing observation in the whole H-SUBSTRATE story (payment layer + condition retained), so its substrate deserves the most independent evidence and has the least.
row 4 — Korea 광범위 항생제처방률 [HIGH] — CIRCULAR. 'Record states KCD J00-J06 for the denominator plus drug-class binding for the numerator' is the outcome restated as substrate evidence.

row 5 — Korea 급성하기도감염(J20-J22) [HIGH] — CIRCULAR. 'The J20-J22 range appears in the indicator name per the record' is purely the outcome. A code range in an indicator's NAME says nothing about the feed it runs on.

row 6 — 의료질평가지원금 [moderate] — DOUBLY DERIVED. 'It fires against the clinician's own diagnostic assessment, which is the record in front of them, so the feed trivially contains the condition.' The measure's own authored value sets are the outcome; inferring the feed from them is the exact prohibited move. row 14 — HEDIS public reporting [moderate] — inherits row 13's circular basis; scan grades it verified='inferred'.
row 15 — CMS Medicaid/CHIP Core Set [moderate] — CIRCULAR. 'The record states the NCQA value sets are adopted wholesale, and those value sets are claims code systems' is again binding-implies-feed.

countryInferredRows: rows 1-6 (all six Korean rows) — substrate rests entirely on the jurisdiction-level fact that Korean NHI 청구명세서 carry mandatory KCD 상병코드. No row cites an instrument-level specification of its own data source. Korea also runs DUR (real-time, prescription-level), NHIS 건강검진/자격 files and survey feeds; a country-level inference cannot distinguish them, and the same six rows would have been coded identically had HIRA computed the indicator off a dispensing extract.
row 6 — 의료질평가지원금: country-level inference stacked on a programme-level inference; the fund's own indicator specification was never reached (analyst states this).

row 9 — MHLW manual: codingPressure='reimbursement-justifying' is explicitly recorded 'on the jurisdiction-level fact that Japanese レセプト require a 傷病名'. The manual is not adjudicated by any payer; the jurisdiction fact has no bearing on it.

row 11 — 抗菌薬適正使用体制加算: codingPressure='reimbursement-justifying' imported from the same jurisdiction fact while the row's own substrate field says the feed carries no patient row at all. Self-contradictory within the row.
row 12 — 感染対策向上加算１: same jurisdiction-level import into a 施設基準 duty that is verified by 届出 and on-site audit, not by claims adjudication.

rows 13-15 (USA) — substrate rests on 'a payer will not adjudicate without a diagnosis', a US-wide claims fact, plus the measure's own value sets. Neither is an instrument-level statement of which feed was used, and the analyst concedes not knowing whether the current HEDIS year is administrative or ECDS — two materially different feeds.

COUNTER-EXAMPLE THE CLASSIFICATION GOT RIGHT — England rows 7 and 8 are correctly assigned different substrates (dispensing-only vs per-pathway fee claim) within one country. This is the one place the analyst resisted country-level inference, and it is also the only place the domain contains within-country substrate variance. Note the consequence: with Korea, Japan-claims and the USA all coded from one country-level premise each, the entire H-SUBSTRATE result rests on about four independent substrate determinations, not seventeen.
shapeErrors: ABSENCE-NUMERATOR ROWS MISCODED AS 'avoidance' — the classification asserts (note 5) that 'no instrument in this domain is undertreatment-shaped'. That is false under the schema's own structural test. H-SEVERABILITY defines the split by what the numerator event is: a drug event that happened, or the ABSENCE of one.

row 13 — HEDIS AAB: the basis states 'the numerator event is a dispensed antibiotic'. This is factually wrong. NCQA AAB is 'the percentage of episodes ... that did NOT result in an antibiotic dispensing event' — a higher rate is better precisely because the numerator is the absence. Delete the acute-bronchitis denominator and 'episodes with no antibiotic' has no population, which is the schema's literal definition of load-bearing. Rows 14 and 15 inherit the same measure and the same error.

row 10 — 耳鼻咽喉科小児抗菌薬適正使用支援加算: the paid act is 'diagnosed acute URI/otitis/sinusitis in a child under 6 AND did not use an antibiotic'. The numerator event is a non-prescription. The analyst correctly called this load-bearing but then coded the shape 'avoidance', which contradicts their own reasoning in the same row.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ARITHMETIC — the blanket 'avoidance' coding is what produced note 2's claim that 'this entire domain is avoidance-shaped, so H-SEVERABILITY has almost no variance to work with here'. The variance was destroyed by the coding, not absent from the data. Corrected, the domain contains 4 absence-numerator rows (10, 13, 14, 15), ALL of which retained the condition axis, versus 13 happened-event rows of which 3 dropped it. H-SEVERABILITY is testable here and directionally supported; the classification as delivered suppressed the only evidence that competes with H-SUBSTRATE.

AMBIGUITY THAT MUST BE RUN BOTH WAYS — the counter-reading is that 'criterionShape' means the shape of the CLINICAL criterion (avoid antibiotics in viral URI), in which case all 17 are avoidance and the absence-numerator property belongs only in conditionRole. I have coded by the numerator test because that is the test the hypothesis text specifies, and because 'undertreatment' there is defined structurally ('the numerator event is the ABSENCE of a drug'), not by clinical desirability. Report both codings; the H-SEVERABILITY verdict for this domain flips between them.

conditionRole FOR THE KOREAN ROWS IS SOUND AND SHOULD NOT BE CHANGED — 'severable-refinement' is not merely a judgement call there, it is empirically demonstrated: England's Quality Premium publishes exactly the condition-free residue (antibiotic items per STAR-PU) and ESAC-Net publishes exactly the condition-free residue of row 4 (broad-spectrum share of total consumption). The severable coding survives note 2's own doubt.

codingPressure IS NOT MEASURING THE CONSTRUCT H-CODING-PRESSURE NAMES (dataset-level, affects rows 1-6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15). The hypothesis distinguishes conditions that JUSTIFY REIMBURSEMENT FOR THE DRUG IN QUESTION (carve-outs) from index conditions naming a hazard. The analyst instead scored 'does this jurisdiction require a diagnosis field on the claim form' — a substrate fact. Under the hypothesis's own definition, J00-J06 / acute bronchitis are hazard indices for which the antibiotic is being DENIED, not approved-indication carve-outs, so nearly every 'reimbursement-justifying' in this domain is mis-scored. Worse, as scored the field is a near-deterministic function of substrate, so H-CODING-PRESSURE cannot be distinguished from H-SUBSTRATE with this data. Only rows 8 (Pharmacy First pathway) and 16 (PBS Indication) are genuinely indication-justifying. Split the field into two before running any arithmetic.

NON-INDEPENDENCE OF ROWS (dataset-level). Rows 1, 2, 3 are three layers of ONE indicator (급성상기도감염 항생제처방률) and rows 13, 14, 15 are three layers of ONE measure (HEDIS AAB). Six of seventeen rows are duplicated observations of two underlying instruments, all in the retained + carries-condition cell. Any exception-free claim ('that holds for all 15/17 instruments without exception') is really a claim about roughly 8-10 independent instruments, of which only 3 are negative cases (England QP, Japan AWaRe add-on, ESAC-Net). Weight or cluster before testing.

ENUM STRAIN CONFIRMED — 'claims-with-diagnosis' is doing two incompatible jobs: a coded-diagnosis administrative feed (Korea, USA) and an adjudicated natural-language / structured-indication field (rows 8, 10, 16). The scan's own newHypotheses C proposes this as a distinct third type. Collapsing them inflates the apparent uniformity of the substrate predictor.

audits.domain: Diabetes medication safety and hypoglycaemia risk in older adults
circularRows: Scotland — 'Polypharmacy Indicators' full specification (ISD Scotland): the ONLY evidence offered for substrate is the record's own binding string saying the denominators run over 'GP record diagnosis codes, lab results and repeat-prescribing data'. That string describes what the indicator does with codes. The indicator's use of coded diagnoses IS the retention outcome, so it cannot establish that the feed would carry conditions for a reason independent of the safety rule. Textbook instance of the circular form.

United States — CMS eCQM CMS122v13 / MIPS #001: substrateCarriesCondition is argued from the fact that the measure's own frailty/advanced-illness EXCLUSION VALUE SETS are ICD-10/SNOMED/HCPCS/CPT. The value sets are the instrument's content, not the feed's content. The independent half of the argument ('US encounters are adjudicated on coded diagnoses') is a country-level generality, not evidence about this feed.

United States — HEDIS GSD: same form. 'the frailty/advanced-illness exclusion value sets are exactly such billed diagnoses, SNF/DME/home-care codes' reads the measure's own specification back as proof of what the substrate carries. Aggravated by the row hedging that GSD is ECDS-style (claims blended with EHR/lab extracts) and then labelling the substrate claims-with-diagnosis anyway.

Korea — HIRA 적정성평가 indicator 11: the cited proof that the claims feed carries conditions is that 'the record itself notes E10–E14 and I10–I13 are authored and applied'. That is the indicator's own code list, i.e. the outcome. The independent premise (HIRA will not adjudicate without KCD codes) is generic to all Korean claims and says nothing about this indicator's actual feed.

United States — PQA/CMS SUPD (the only confidence:'high' row): INVERSE circularity. The clause 'this is why the denominator condition is built from antidiabetic medication fills rather than from a diagnosis code list' derives the substrate from the observed substitution, which is precisely the retention outcome. The genuinely independent premise (Part D PDE records have no diagnosis field) is correct but is unverified prior knowledge — no specification was read this session — so it cannot carry a 'high' rating on its own.
countryInferredRows: Scotland — National Therapeutic Indicator 'Increase Falls Risk: Sulfonylurea use in frail older adults': substrate assigned from 'my knowledge of the PIS-based NTI publication series', i.e. from the programme family, not this indicator. Scotland demonstrably runs both PIS-computed national indicators and GP-system case-finding indicators, so the programme-level inference is exactly the inference this audit disallows. Additionally unresolved: an indicator whose title names frailty must represent frailty somehow; the actual proxy was never established.

Scotland — Quality Prescribing for T2DM 2024–2027 NTI set: the row itself admits these guides carry BOTH PIS-computed NTIs and practice-system case-finding indicators, then assigns a single dispensing-only label anyway. Substrate is unidentified, not dispensing-only.

England — NICE IND179 and IND180: substrate inferred from the class ('NICE general-practice indicators are specified to be computable from the GP clinical system record'), not from either indicator's own specification. England simultaneously runs GP-extract, hospital and ePACT2 dispensing instruments, so class-level inference is not sufficient, though it is the weakest instance in this list.

England and Wales — National Diabetes Audit: labelled 'registry' on programme-level reasoning while the row concedes the upstream feed is the GP EHR and that whether the extract transmits frailty codes is unestablished. The substrate label and the substrateCarriesCondition flag are therefore both national-programme inferences.

Korea — HIRA indicator 11: substrate 'claims-with-diagnosis' is inferred from the general fact that HIRA appropriateness evaluations run on 요양급여비용 청구자료. The row's own caveat refutes it — a HbA1c CONTROL RATE requires a numeric lab value, which is not a claims field, so the operative feed must be a supplementary institution-level clinical submission. The country-level inference contradicts the instrument's own data requirements.

United States — HEDIS GSD: 'HEDIS is computed by health plans over member claims/encounter data' is a programme-level default applied over the row's own acknowledgement that GSD is ECDS-style with clinical/lab supplements.

Germany — G-BA DMP-A-RL Anlage 8: 'registry' and substrateCarriesCondition:true both rest on general knowledge of the eDMP documentation programme, with an explicit admission that Anlage 8's current field inventory was not opened.
shapeErrors: SYSTEMATIC: seven rows whose numerator event is a LABORATORY VALUE, not a prescription, are labelled 'undertreatment' or 'dose-adjustment' — IND179, IND180, QOF DM020/DM021, NDA Report 1, CMS122v13, HEDIS GSD, Korea indicator 11. Applying the stated test (did a prescription happen, or did it not happen?), none of these has a prescription in either numerator or numerator-absence. They are target-attainment rates over an HbA1c result. Labelling them undertreatment/dose-adjustment imports a drug-axis shape the instruments do not have, and it inflates precisely the cells H-SEVERABILITY is tested on.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY in the shape split: IND179 (tight-target half) is coded undertreatment while IND180 (relaxed-target half of the SAME indicator pair, same feed, same numerator type) is coded dose-adjustment; QOF DM020/DM021 — an identical tight/relaxed pair — is coded dose-adjustment as a single row. The same construct receives three different labels depending on which half the analyst looked at. Whatever convention is adopted, it must be applied uniformly; at present the shape variable is partly an artefact of row granularity.

CMS816v4 (Hospital Harm – Severe Hypoglycemia): conditionRole 'severable-refinement' is scored against a condition that the row's own basis says is not in the instrument ('the denominator is drug exposure with no risk condition'). Scoring severability on an absent axis manufactures a supporting data point for H-SEVERABILITY out of nothing. Should be not-applicable.

HEDIS EDH: same counterfactual error — 'any such stratifier WOULD be severable' is scored as if an observed property. The axis actually present in the definition is the coded hypoglycaemia diagnosis in the numerator (and diabetes in the denominator); delete it and the numerator event ceases to exist, which is the load-bearing pattern, not the severable one.

codingPressure 'reimbursement-justifying' is applied to HAZARD conditions (frailty, advanced illness) in CMS122v13, HEDIS GSD, HEDIS EDH and CMS816v4. H-CODING-PRESSURE defines that value as conditions that justify reimbursement FOR THE DRUG IN QUESTION (carve-out/indication codes). Frailty and advanced illness justify reimbursement for other services (SNF, DME, home care), never for the antidiabetic. Under the hypothesis's own definition these are index conditions and must not be scored reimbursement-justifying. As coded, four of the strongest US rows are pre-loaded in the hypothesis's favour. The enum lacks a 'payer-coded-for-a-different-service' value; that gap should be fixed rather than resolved by defaulting upward.

AXIS MISMATCH WITHIN ROWS: substrateCarriesCondition is scored against the INDICATION axis (diabetes coded in claims/EHR) while conditionRole and codingPressure are scored against the HAZARD axis (frailty, dementia, advanced illness) in Korea, NDA, CMS122v13, GSD and Germany Anlage 8. H-SUBSTRATE's predictor and the retention outcome are therefore measured on two different variables in those rows, and any correlation computed across them is uninterpretable. Convention #1 in the notes is stated but not applied consistently — SUPD is scored on the indication axis while Korea, a structurally identical indication-denominator rule, is scored on the absent hazard axis.

The targeting rule is a CONJUNCTION of multiple chronic diseases AND multiple Part D drugs AND a projected cost threshold; deleting the disease prong still leaves a computable eligible population. 'Load-bearing-denominator' was assigned to the two rows that carry the domain's headline retained=true result at payment/rating layers.

The non-circular version of this claim requires showing the underlying criterion cannot be computed without asthma, not that the published one is register-denominated.

SCHEME-LEVEL, the decisive finding: conditionRole reproduces the outcome almost perfectly. load-bearing-denominator 5/5 retained=true; severable-refinement 1/11 retained=true; not-applicable 2/2 retained=true; exclusion-carveout 1/1 retained=true. Mapping not-applicable and exclusion-carveout to 'axis present', the field concords with the outcome on 18 of 19 non-unknown rows. A field coded by an analyst who could see conditionAxisRetained in the same source record, and which separates that outcome at p<0.001, cannot be treated as an independent predictor. substrateCarriesCondition is far less contaminated (true: 8/14 retained; false: 2/7 retained) and is the only field in this batch worth pooling.

It is true and it is the only codingPressure variation in the domain, but it is confounded 1:1 with jurisdiction, so it can carry no weight in the arithmetic - any Scotland/England difference is equally an explanation.

The programme guidance delegates target-setting to hospitals, so no national feed exists to characterise; the row's own conditionRole is correctly left unknown, and substrate should be held at the same standard.
shapeErrors: Blanket 'avoidance' over a heterogeneous multi-item set (Scotland STU, Scotland NTI, Scotland PIS Table E1). The source domain record states 42 of 69 case-finding indicators use diagnosis, examination signs AND laboratory data. A set of that size characteristically contains lab-threshold monitoring items and absence-numerator items (a hazard drug present alongside a protective drug that is missing - gastroprotection, bone protection). Applying the required test - is the numerator event a prescription that happened or one that did not? - to the set as a whole is impossible; it must be applied item by item. This single aggregation is what produces the classifier's claim that the domain contributes 'almost no undertreatment-shaped instruments', which then hollows out the entire H-SEVERABILITY test.

The one row that breaks the perfect conditionRole/outcome mapping is Scotland STU (severable-refinement, retained=true) - and it is precisely the row whose shape was mis-aggregated. If the STU set is undertreatment-heavy, H-SEVERABILITY predicts it correctly and the domain's evidence changes sign. No arithmetic should be run on this domain until the STU/PIS item-level shapes are resolved.

Scotland National Therapeutic Indicators coded 'avoidance' although they are comparative prescribing-volume and drug-count indicators with no drug-in-condition avoidance rule anywhere in them. The correct code under this scheme's own usage is 'other', the same code given to the Japanese drug-count fees.

IIF RESP-01 and RESP-02 bundled into one row with one substrate, one shape and one conditionRole, while the basis admits it cannot tell which of the pair is the over-prescribing volume element and which is the review element. A control case that cannot be decomposed is not a control case.

IIF SMR-02A-D left criterionShape=unknown and conditionRole=unknown on a plea of exhausted search budget, when the dataset's OWN domain verdict field states the content: 'England's four money-bearing SMR-02 indicators are drug-drug pairs plus age'. This is under-use of in-hand evidence, not genuine unknowability. Caveat on the fix: if any pair is specified as a risky combination 'without gastroprotection', the numerator contains an absence and the row is part-undertreatment - which would matter more than any other single fact in this domain.

The Japanese deprescribing fees have an ABSENCE numerator (>=2 fewer internal medicines at discharge - the payable event is a drug that is no longer prescribed) yet the severability argument treats absence as freely computable. They are the exact mirror of the undertreatment case: absence with a drug-count-defined rather than condition-defined population. That is the structure that discriminates H-SEVERABILITY, and coding them 'other' with no comment makes it invisible.

SMR-03 has the same property: a monitoring numerator is a test that did NOT occur. By the scheme's own 'absence has no population' logic it is undertreatment-adjacent and escapes only because its population is drug-defined. The row is defensible but the reasoning should be recorded, since it is the general escape route for every monitoring rule in the scan.

conditionRole 'load-bearing-denominator' applied to DISJUNCTIVE or CONJUNCTIVE eligibility rules (DES SMR cohorts, SMR-01, Part D MTM) where non-condition prongs - care-home residence, >=10 medicines, projected cost threshold - independently yield a computable denominator. Load-bearing requires that no computable population survives deletion; that was asserted for all three and is false for all three.

Internal inconsistency: Poly-ACH/Poly-CNS is coded substrate 'dispensing-only' together with substrateCarriesCondition=true. Under the field's stated definition (the feed the instrument is actually computed over) those two values cannot both hold.

codingPressure was deliberately recorded at health-system level rather than feed-and-condition level, making it a near-constant: 18 of 21 rows reimbursement-justifying, and all 3 exceptions are Scotland. The field therefore has zero within-jurisdiction variance and cannot test H-CODING-PRESSURE at all. Worse, the hypothesis is defined per CONDITION (does this condition justify reimbursement for THIS drug), so the recorded values answer a different question. Only OMP's cancer carve-out, and arguably the QOF asthma register, are genuinely payment-forced at the condition level in this batch.

Coverage misstatement: the note claims 'all 21 instruments in element 5 classified'. The source domain holds 23. The two dropped rows - IIF 2023/24 removal of all SMR incentives, and HIRA 요양급여 적정성평가 P4P - are exactly the two whose conditionAxisRetained is null. Selecting the analysed sample on the outcome field, undeclared, is a selection defect independent of any row-level error.

Non-independence: the レセプト記載要領 row is the claim-form encoding of the A250/B008-2 fees already counted, giving Japan a third condition-free payment observation that is a derivative of the first two. Likewise the Scotland STU and PIS rows are one rule family on two feeds - an excellent paired contrast, but two dependent draws. Pooling all 21 as independent overstates n by at least two.
