(a) severability 'demonstrated' by PINCER's sibling drug-only indicators, i.e. by other instruments' retention outcomes; (b) substrateCarriesCondition=true rests substantially on the indicator's own denominator using EGFR_COD, which is the outcome. The independent leg (eGFR present as routine U&E reporting) is asserted, not sourced, and the cited MIQUEST field 'Latest Renal Function Code 15M-0M' is a field written for this query library, so it is rule-dependent rather than rule-independent evidence.

Scotland — Public Health Scotland NTIs: analyst admits criterionShape and conditionRole were 'assigned from the domain's underlying clinical rule rather than from a read of any individual renal NTI.' The fields were back-filled from what the instrument is known to lack. Imputation into a predictor column, in a domain where the outcome is already known.

Netherlands — Richtlijn CNS: substrate=ehr-record is imported from a different instrument (the G-Standaard, retained=true) that this prose guideline delegates to. Borrowing a downstream retained instrument's feed to score an upstream guideline's substrate is circularity via transitivity.

England — NICE IND232: conditionRole=load-bearing-denominator tracks the presence of EGFR_COD in the parent scan's binding field, which is the same code-presence signal the scan used to set retained=true. Predictor and outcome are being read off one artefact.
countryInferredRows: England — QOF CKD domain: substrate 'well established generically' from how QOF instruments are computed as a class, not from this instrument's own data source. The parent scan flags the row 'inferred' and no CKD business rules were obtained. Worse, the basis concedes there is no CKD drug-safety indicator at all — so there is no instrument here whose substrate could be observed.

Netherlands — Richtlijn CNS: substrate assigned from the Dutch health-IT landscape (huisarts/apotheek/secondary-care systems) rather than from any feed this guideline computes over. It computes nothing. Compare the two other non-computing prose guidances in the same domain, Scotland's 2018 guidance body and Japan's MHLW 指針, both correctly coded unknown. Three instruments of identical type, two coded unknown, one coded ehr-record — the inconsistency is unexplained and it inflates the ehr-record cell.

Netherlands — KNMP G-Standaard: substrate=ehr-record is a country/system-level collapse. The row's own basis states the surveillance runs in both huisarts/hospital records AND pharmacy AIS. Those are different feed types with, by the analyst's own account, opposite carriage answers. Leaving substrateCarriesCondition null while hard-coding substrate to a single ehr-record value is internally inconsistent: if the arms differ on carriage they differ on substrate.
shapeErrors: NICE IND232 — role misassigned. Numerator event is a prescription/test that HAPPENED (an eGFR measurement existing), in a drug-defined denominator (long-term oral NSAID). No eGFR threshold is ever tested. So the kidney axis enters as a measurement act, never as a population condition. Deleting the condition-as-attribute leaves the measure fully computable; what is load-bearing is the eGFR TEST, not the eGFR VALUE. conditionRole must be severable-refinement. This single change is also the only thing that breaks the shape→role identity map, so it materially changes any H-SEVERABILITY arithmetic.

NICE IND232 — upstream outcome error implied. If retained=true was set because EGFR_COD appears in the binding, the outcome variable is measuring code presence, not condition-axis survival. This instrument never conditions on kidney function; the criterion mutated from value-conditioned contraindication to test-existence monitoring. The parent scan's retained=true should be re-examined, and the analyst noted the shape mutation without following it through to the outcome flag.

Wales AWTTC NPIs — shape is not defined at row level. The row bundles multiple Prescribing Safety Indicators of different shapes, and was coded on 'the dominant avoidance shape.' The bundle explicitly contains a monitoring indicator (75+ on ACEi/loop diuretic WITHOUT a renal check in 15 months) whose numerator event is a prescription/test that did NOT happen — the absence shape. Dominant-shape coding silently discards the one arm that discriminates between the hypotheses. Split the row per indicator.
Public Health Scotland NTIs — shape and role are imputed, not observed. 92+17 indicators, no individual renal NTI read. Both fields must be unknown.

South Korea HIRA DUR — shape fabricated from the domain header. The instrument implements no renal rule whatsoever; the nine DUR categories contain nothing renal. criterionShape=dose-adjustment and conditionRole=load-bearing describe a criterion this instrument never encodes. This is not a minor point: the notes present Korea as the honest counterexample that 'cuts against H-SEVERABILITY,' so the classification's own circularity-guard proof rests on an imputed value. Correct it and the counterexample disappears, leaving the guard unevidenced.

Japan MHLW 別表3 — role contradicted by the artefact. conditionRole=load-bearing is derived from Giusti-Hayton arithmetic, but the published artefact is a two-column drug list with no thresholds, i.e. a fully publishable output with the condition deleted. That is a demonstration of severability at the instrument level. Row is criterion-level coding masquerading as instrument-level; already low confidence, but the direction of the error should be recorded.

Structural — conditionRole is a deterministic function of criterionShape across all 13 rows (avoidance→severable, monitoring/dose-adjustment→load-bearing, other→n/a). It is a relabeling, not an observation. Likewise substrateCarriesCondition is a deterministic function of substrate across all 13. Neither H-SUBSTRATE nor H-SEVERABILITY can be tested against this coding as written; the arithmetic afterwards will only recover the substrate and shape columns.

Scotland 2018 guidance body — shape 'mixed avoidance/dose-adjustment/monitoring, coded on the dominant avoidance form.' Same dominant-shape problem as Wales. Confidence is already low so no correction issued, but the row should not enter any shape-based tabulation.

No undertreatment-shaped instrument exists anywhere in this domain (0/13). H-SEVERABILITY's central contrast — undertreatment rules cannot shed the condition, avoidance rules can — is therefore untestable in domain index 2. Any apparent support here is carried entirely by the dose-adjustment/monitoring rows, which is a different mechanism from the one the hypothesis states.

corrections.instrument: England — NHSBSA/NHS Digital Medication Safety Indicators, AKI01
corrections.to: linked dispensing + admitted-patient-care (claims-with-diagnosis arm present); split the row by arm
corrections.why: The row's own basis states the admission-rate variant links to HES Admitted Patient Care by NHS number and applies ICD-10 N170-N179/O904. A feed carrying ICD-10 codes is not dispensing-only. The analyst excluded those codes on the ground that they are the AKI outcome rather than the index condition — a valid distinction for conditionRole, but not for substrate, which asks what the feed carries, not what the rule uses. Note the inconsistency: the Netherlands G-Standaard row was left null precisely because it runs in two arms with opposite answers, while AKI01's two arms were collapsed in the direction that preserves H-SUBSTRATE. Apply the same rule to both.

corrections.instrument: England — NHSBSA/NHS Digital Medication Safety Indicators, AKI01
corrections.to: null (contested; true for the HES-linked arm)
corrections.why: If the linked feed demonstrably carries coded diagnoses and the instrument still substituted a drug-only triple-therapy definition, this row is a counterexample to H-SUBSTRATE rather than a confirmation of it. Coding it false converts the single most informative row in the domain into supporting evidence. This is the most consequential correction in the audit.

corrections.instrument: England — NHSBSA/NHS Digital Medication Safety Indicators, AKI01
corrections.why: High confidence is not defensible on a row whose substrate category is contradicted by a code list named in its own basis, and whose conditionRole basis is explicitly outcome-derived ('severable by demonstration').

corrections.instrument: United States — NCQA HEDIS DDE Rate 3 (CKD × NSAIDs)
corrections.to: encounter-adjudication-only (not drug-justifying); code unknown if the schema lacks the value
corrections.why: Internal contradiction: the basis itself concludes 'CKD is a hazard here, not an indication for the NSAID, so the pressure is generic-encounter pressure, not drug-justifying pressure' — and then codes reimbursement-justifying anyway. H-CODING-PRESSURE defines reimbursement-justifying as a condition that justifies reimbursement for the drug in question; CKD does not justify an NSAID. Under the hypothesis's own carve-out/index split, CKD is an index hazard condition and belongs in the unpressured arm. This is the ONLY claims-with-diagnosis row and the ONLY reimbursement-justifying row in the domain, so the miscoding manufactures an n=1 confirmation of H-CODING-PRESSURE out of a row that, correctly coded, is a refutation (unpressured index condition, retained=true). The schema also lacks a value for payer-forced-but-not-drug-forced coding; flag that gap rather than rounding it to the nearest hypothesis-friendly value.

corrections.instrument: England — NICE indicator IND232
corrections.why: The numerator event is an eGFR measurement that HAPPENED; the denominator is drug-defined (long-term oral NSAID). No kidney-function threshold is ever tested, so the condition never enters as a population attribute — only the CKD register appears, as a severable denominator exclusion whose deletion still leaves a computable rate. The analyst identified the competing reading and chose the one that preserves the shape→role identity map. Correcting this row is the only thing in the domain that makes conditionRole non-redundant.

corrections.instrument: England — NICE indicator IND232
corrections.why: The row's own basis records that the criterion mutated shape (contraindication → monitoring) between source guidance and instrument, and that the two role readings disagree. It is also the row where the parent scan's retained=true may reflect nothing more than EGFR_COD appearing in the binding. Predictor and outcome are being read off the same artefact; low is the honest level until the outcome flag is re-derived.

corrections.instrument: Netherlands — Federatie Medisch Specialisten Richtlijn CNS
corrections.why: The instrument is prose guidance that, by its own basis, 'computes nothing itself and authors no binding.' It has no substrate. The ehr-record value was imported from the G-Standaard, a separate instrument in the same domain that is coded retained=true. Scotland's 2018 guidance body and Japan's MHLW 指針 are the same instrument type and were correctly coded unknown; there is no stated reason for treating this one differently.

corrections.instrument: Netherlands — Federatie Medisch Specialisten Richtlijn CNS
corrections.why: Follows from substrate=unknown. A non-computing guideline has no feed to carry anything, and asserting true here adds a spurious ehr-record/carries-true/retained-true row to the cell that H-SUBSTRATE is scored on.

corrections.instrument: Netherlands — Federatie Medisch Specialisten Richtlijn CNS
corrections.why: Every substrate-side property on this row is inferred from a different instrument.

corrections.instrument: Netherlands — KNMP G-Standaard
corrections.to: mixed (ehr-record + pharmacy dispensing system); split the row by arm
corrections.why: The basis states outright that the surveillance is built into both huisarts/hospital prescribing systems and pharmacy AIS, and that the arms differ on whether the clearance value is present for rule-independent reasons. The analyst correctly refused to collapse substrateCarriesCondition to a boolean but then collapsed substrate itself to a single value, which decides by the back door the same question the null was protecting. Split the row, as the notes themselves recommend.

corrections.instrument: Netherlands — KNMP G-Standaard
corrections.why: An unsplit two-arm row cannot support moderate confidence on a field whose value differs by arm.

corrections.instrument: Scotland — Public Health Scotland National Therapeutic Indicators
corrections.why: Admitted imputation: no individual renal NTI was read, the indicator lookup file could not be downloaded, and the value was assigned from the domain's underlying clinical rule. A predictor filled in from the domain header in a scan where the outcome is already known is not an observation.

corrections.instrument: Scotland — Public Health Scotland National Therapeutic Indicators
corrections.why: Derived entirely from the imputed criterionShape. Substrate and substrateCarriesCondition on this row are firm and should be retained; only the shape/role pair is unsupported.

corrections.instrument: South Korea — HIRA/MFDS DUR
corrections.why: The instrument encodes no renal rule at all — the nine DUR categories are exhaustive and contain nothing renal or diagnosis-conditioned. Coding a shape here describes a criterion the instrument never implements, imported from the domain title. Critically, the classification's notes cite this row as proof the circularity guard worked ('Korea, retained false, lands on load-bearing, which cuts against H-SEVERABILITY'). That proof is built on an imputed value; corrected, it evaporates, and the guard is left without a demonstration.

corrections.instrument: South Korea — HIRA/MFDS DUR
corrections.why: Follows from criterionShape=unknown.

corrections.instrument: South Korea — HIRA/MFDS DUR
corrections.why: substrateCarriesCondition=false is inferred from the absence of a renal check category, which is the retention outcome. The independent claim — that the real-time DUR transaction message carries no KCD 상병코드 and no lab result — is asserted without a read of the DUR message specification. The distinction between the DUR transaction feed and the downstream 요양급여비용 claim is exactly right and worth keeping, but it needs the message schema behind it to justify high.

corrections.instrument: England — Quality and Outcomes Framework, CKD domain
corrections.from: included as an instrument in domain index 2 (counts toward the retention denominator)
corrections.to: excluded, or carried as a documented null with all predictor fields unknown
corrections.why: The basis establishes that no CKD drug-safety indicator conditioned on kidney function exists in QOF: there is a register used as a CHOL003 denominator component and nothing else. A register is case-identification, not a medication-safety instrument, which is why criterionShape had to be coded 'other' and conditionRole 'not-applicable.' Scoring retained=false against an instrument that was never in this domain injects a false negative into the payment layer — the layer H-SUBSTRATE makes its boldest prediction about — and it is simultaneously the sole ehr-record row discordant with retention, i.e. the one row propping the substrate→retention fit at 11/13 rather than a suspiciously clean 11/12. It is also the only row in the domain with no primary document behind it. Either exclude it or re-scan it against the actual QOF business rules before any arithmetic is run.

corrections.instrument: Wales — AWTTC National Prescribing Indicators 2025-2026
corrections.to: moderate (shape and role only; substrate stays high)
corrections.why: Substrate is the best-evidenced in the entire domain — the in-document contrast between 'Data source: DHCW' and 'Data source: NWSSP' establishes the feed at instrument level with no country-level inference, and it should be held up as the standard the other rows failed to meet. But the row bundles several indicators of differing shapes and was coded on the dominant one, discarding a monitoring indicator whose numerator event is an absence. Shape and role cannot carry high confidence at row level; split the bundle per indicator.
